definition_zh: 有韧性的；能弹回的；受扰动后能迅速恢复的
definition_en: able to spring back into shape after being bent or pressed, and able to recover quickly after damage or stress
core_image: 一根被洪水压弯的柳枝在松手后弹回原形，枝条上还挂着没掉的水珠
scene: 洪水退去的河滩上，一棵被冲得贴地的柳树在第二年春天又直起了腰，枝条上抽满新叶。A willow flattened by the flood straightened within a season, a sign that the riverside woodland is resilient.
sceneCN: 这里 resilient 指「受扰动后能恢复原状」（第 2 个义项：生态系统在受损或受压后回到原有结构与功能）；句意：被洪水压平的柳树在一个季节内重新挺直，说明这片河岸林地具有恢复力。图中可辨识物件：贴地的柳干、新抽的枝条、退水后留下的泥痕、远处的河岸。

pos.zh: 有韧性的；能弹回的；能迅速恢复的（比较级 more resilient，最高级 most resilient）

senses.title: Springing back after being bent
senses.titleCN: 弹回：被压弯后恢复原形
senses.definition: able to return to an original shape after being bent, stretched or compressed
senses.definitionCN: 被弯曲、拉伸或压缩之后能够回到原来形状的
senses.example: Rubber is resilient enough to return to its shape after a hard squeeze.
senses.exampleCN: 橡胶的弹性足以在用力挤压后恢复原状。
senses.why: re- marks a movement back and salire means to leap, so the word describes a leap back into place.
senses.whyCN: re- 表示「回到」，salire 意为「跳」，因此这个词描述的是「跳回原位」。

senses.title: Recovering after a disturbance
senses.titleCN: 受扰后恢复：回到原有结构与功能
senses.definition: able to recover its former structure and function after damage or disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 在受损或受扰动之后能恢复到原有结构与功能的
senses.example: The riverside woodland proved resilient and regrew within two seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 这片河岸林地表现出恢复力，两个季节内就重新长了起来。
senses.why: ecology borrowed the springing-back image and applied it to a whole system rather than a single object.
senses.whyCN: 生态学借用了「弹回」这个形象，把它从单个物体扩展到整个系统。

senses.title: Bouncing back from a setback
senses.titleCN: 挫折后振作：人从打击中站起
senses.definition: able to recover quickly from hardship, failure or emotional shock
senses.definitionCN: 能从困苦、失败或情绪冲击中迅速恢复的
senses.example: After losing the season's crop, the farmers stayed resilient and replanted.
senses.exampleCN: 这一季的收成没了，农民们仍然振作，重新种了下去。
senses.why: the same rebound is read on a personal scale: a mind that bends under pressure and then straightens again.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「回弹」被放到个人尺度上：心志受压弯下，随后又挺直。

senses.title: Absorbing stress without breaking
senses.titleCN: 抗压不折：受力而不断裂
senses.definition: strong enough to take repeated stress without permanent damage
senses.definitionCN: 足以承受反复应力而不留下永久损伤的
senses.example: The bridge's resilient joints flex in an earthquake instead of cracking.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥的韧性接缝在地震中弯而不裂。
senses.why: a material that springs back also survives the force, so resilience comes to mean toughness under load.
senses.whyCN: 能弹回的材料也就能扛住那股力，于是恢复力引申为承载下的韧性。

senses.title: Adapting to change without losing function
senses.titleCN: 适应变化：换条件仍能运转
senses.definition: able to adjust to new conditions while keeping essential functions
senses.definitionCN: 能够调整以适应新条件、同时保住核心功能的
senses.example: A resilient economy shifts its supply chains instead of collapsing.
senses.exampleCN: 有韧性的经济会调整供应链，而不是直接崩掉。
senses.why: if a system can bend and still return, then change itself need not destroy it; adjustment replaces collapse.
senses.whyCN: 既然系统能弯而仍能回位，变化本身就不必毁掉它；调整取代了崩溃。

senses.title: Returning to a reference state in ecology
senses.titleCN: 生态回复：扰动后回到参照状态
senses.definition: in ecology, the capacity of a system to return to a reference state after a disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中指系统受扰动后回到某一参照状态的能力
senses.example: Researchers measured how resilient the grassland was after heavy grazing.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者测量了重牧之后这片草地的回复能力。
senses.why: the technical sense fixes what counts as back: not any new state, but the one recorded before the disturbance.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语义限定「回」到哪：不是随便一个新状态，而是扰动前记录的那个状态。

senses.title: Tough yet flexible, not brittle
senses.titleCN: 韧而不脆：能弯不易碎
senses.definition: describing a material that deforms readily but resists fracture
senses.definitionCN: 形容容易变形却不易断裂的材料
senses.example: Willow is resilient, which is why baskets are woven from its stems.
senses.exampleCN: 柳木有韧性，所以人们用它的枝条编筐。
senses.why: brittle things snap where resilient things give, so the word contrasts flexibility with fracture.
senses.whyCN: 脆的东西一压就断，有韧性的东西则先让一步，因此这个词把柔性与断裂对立起来。

senses.title: Enduring repeated shocks
senses.titleCN: 反复受冲击仍存续
senses.definition: able to keep going through one shock after another over a long period
senses.definitionCN: 在长时期内经受一次又一次冲击而仍能维持的
senses.example: The coastal fishery stayed resilient through three poor years in a row.
senses.exampleCN: 这片沿海渔场连续三年歉收仍然撑住了。
senses.why: one rebound is elasticity; many rebounds in succession become endurance, the abstract extension of the same image.
senses.whyCN: 一次回弹是弹性，接连多次回弹便成了耐久，这是同一意象的抽象延伸。

intro.en: Resilient comes from Latin resilire 'to leap back', built on re- 'back' and salire 'to leap'. The earliest English uses are dated to the seventeenth century, and the dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: resilient 出自拉丁 resilire「跳回」，由 re-「向后」与 salire「跳」构成。英语最早用例定在 17 世纪，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: The verb salire meant 'to leap, jump', and it also supplied salient 'leaping out' and assault 'a leaping at'. Its own earlier origin is not settled.
items.cn: 动词 salire 意为「跳、跃」，它还派生出 salient「跃出的」与 assault「扑向」；其更早的来源并无定论。

items.en: Adding re- 'back' produced resilire 'to leap back, recoil', used of things that bend and then return.
items.cn: 加上 re-「向后」得到 resilire「跳回、反冲」，用于描写弯曲后又回位的东西。

items.en: Resilient entered English in the 1670s, first describing bodies that spring back after compression. The exact first citation is uncertain.
items.cn: resilient 于 17 世纪 70 年代进入英语，最初描写受压后弹回的物体；确切的最早书证不确定。

items.en: By the 1830s the word was applied to persons and institutions that recover readily from hardship.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪 30 年代，这个词被用于形容能迅速从困苦中恢复的人与机构。

items.en: C. S. Holling's 1973 paper on ecological resilience fixed the technical sense: the capacity to absorb disturbance and still retain function.
items.cn: C. S. Holling 1973 年关于生态恢复力的论文确定了术语义：吸收扰动后仍保持功能的能力。

items.en: First dates are approximate; the shift from physical elasticity to social recovery cannot be pinned to a single text.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数；从物理弹性到社会性恢复的语义转移无法锁定到某一具体文本。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes of different origin that share the re- prefix; group two holds near meanings with a different core image.
note.cn: 第一组是同带 re- 前缀但来源不同的形近词；第二组是核心意象不同的近义词。

entries.definition: Able to withstand an force without giving way. It comes from resistere 'to stand against' and contains no idea of returning.
entries.definitionCN: 指能顶住外力而不退让，出自 resistere「站住对抗」，不含「回位」之意。

entries.tag: the noun of the same word
entries.definition: The capacity named by resilient. The two differ only in part of speech, not in image.
entries.definitionCN: resilient 所表能力的名词形式；二者只差词性，意象相同。

entries.definition: To spring back or withdraw, taken straight from Latin resilire. It is rare and mostly legal in English.
entries.definitionCN: 直接取自拉丁 resilire 的「弹回、撤回」，英语中罕用，多见于法律文本。

entries.definition: From Latin resultare 'to spring back', but it settled on 'what follows from something', not on elasticity.
entries.definitionCN: 出自拉丁 resultare「弹回」，但词义落在「由某事产生的结果」上，而非弹性。

entries.definition: Returns to shape after stretching, but says nothing about recovery of a whole system or a person.
entries.definitionCN: 指拉伸后恢复形状，但不涉及整个系统或人的恢复。

entries.definition: Strong and hard to damage. It stresses withstanding force, while resilient stresses recovering afterwards.
entries.definitionCN: 指结实、难损坏，强调顶住外力；resilient 强调事后的恢复。

entries.definition: Able to change to fit new conditions. It describes the change itself, not the return to a former state.
entries.definitionCN: 指能改变以适合新条件，描述改变本身，而非回到原状态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' + salire 'leap': something that leaps back into shape.
normal.cn: re-「回」+ salire「跳」：能跳回原形的东西。

normal.en: The family runs resilient, resilience, resiliency, resiliently, resile.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 resilient、resilience、resiliency、resiliently、resile。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: resilient ecosystem, resilient community, resilient economy, resilient to stress.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：有恢复力的生态系统、有抗逆力的社区、有韧性的经济、对压力有承受力。

normal.en: Ecology pairs it with disturbance: a system absorbs the shock and then returns.
normal.cn: 生态学把它与扰动配对：系统先吸收冲击，再回位。

normal.en: Materials pair it with brittle: resilient bends, brittle snaps.
normal.cn: 材料学把它与脆性对举：韧性弯而不折，脆性一压就断。

abstract.en: Picture a reed that lies flat in a flood and stands up again when the water drops.
abstract.cn: 想象一根芦苇在洪水里贴地倒下，水退后又立起来。

abstract.en: Picture a spring compressed under a weight, waiting to release.
abstract.cn: 想象一根被重物压住的弹簧，蓄着回弹的力。

abstract.en: Picture a community that rebuilds its market on the same square after every storm.
abstract.cn: 想象一个社区每次风暴过后都在同一个广场上重建市集。

examples.en: The grassland is resilient enough to recover from a single dry year.
examples.cn: 这片草地恢复力足够强，能熬过一个干旱年份。

examples.en: Children who are resilient often have one stable adult in their lives.
examples.cn: 有抗逆力的孩子往往生活里有一位稳定的成年人。

examples.en: Engineers tested how resilient the alloy was under repeated loading.
examples.cn: 工程师测试了这种合金在反复加载下的韧性。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「日（re）里筛（sil）→ 被筛得弯了还能弹回来」——受压回弹、受扰恢复 → 有韧性、恢复力强

root: 拉丁 re-「向后」+ salire「跳」→ resilire「跳回、反冲」；英语 resilient 于 17 世纪由该词根进入，生态学术语义由 20 世纪固定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is bent or hit, gives way, and then leaps back, first as a shape, then as a system, a person, a material and a long-run capacity.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：某物被压弯或击中，先让一步，再弹回来；先指形状，再指系统、人、材料与长期能力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bent branch that straightens itself once the load is gone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根被压弯的枝条，外力一去便自行挺直。

branches.en: PHYSICAL REBOUND: the literal leap back, first of a body and then of a whole ecosystem.
branches.cn: 物理回弹：字面的跳回，先指物体，再指整个生态系统。

branches.en: PERSONAL TOUGHNESS: a mind or a structure takes the blow and straightens again.
branches.cn: 个体韧性：心志或结构承受打击后再度挺直。

branches.en: ADAPTIVE FLEX: change is met by adjustment rather than collapse.
branches.cn: 适应性柔度：以调整而非崩溃来应对变化。

branches.en: ECOLOGICAL RETURN: the system comes back to a recorded reference state.
branches.cn: 生态回复：系统回到有记录的参照状态。

branches.en: ENDURANCE: flexibility in the material and repetition over time turn rebound into lasting capacity.
branches.cn: 耐久：材料层面的柔性与时间上的重复，把回弹变成持久能力。

intro.en: The adjective is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin verb stem; its endings -ent and -ence are the usual adjective and noun markers.
intro.cn: 这个形容词由拉丁前缀加拉丁动词词干构成；词尾 -ent 与 -ence 是常见的形容词与名词标记。

latinIntro.en: Latin salire 'to leap' yields resilient, resilience, resile and, through resultare, result; the same stem appears in assault and salient.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 salire「跳」衍生 resilient、resilience、resile，并经 resultare 衍生 result；同一词干还出现在 assault 与 salient 中。

items.example: The reed bed is resilient after cutting.
items.exampleCN: 这片芦苇地在收割后仍有恢复力。

items.example: Ecologists study the resilience of coral reefs.
items.exampleCN: 生态学家研究珊瑚礁的恢复力。

items.meaningCN: 恢复力（主要用于美式英语）
items.example: The agency measured community resiliency.
items.exampleCN: 该机构测量了社区的抗逆力。

items.example: The crop recovered resiliently after hail.
items.exampleCN: 冰雹过后作物有韧性地恢复了。

items.example: The contract resiled to its earlier terms.
items.exampleCN: 合同回退到先前的条款。

items.meaning: that which springs back from an act; an outcome
items.meaningCN: 由某一行为弹回之物；结果
items.example: The flood was the result of three days of rain.
items.exampleCN: 这场洪水是三天降雨的结果。

items.example: The storm assaulted the coast for a full night.
items.exampleCN: 风暴整夜猛扑海岸。

items.example: The salient feature of the valley is its dry floor.
items.exampleCN: 这条谷地最显著的特征是干涸的谷底。

definition_zh: 干扰；扰动；扰乱；（生态）扰动事件
definition_en: the act of interrupting order or peace, and in ecology any event that changes the structure of a habitat
core_image: 平静的湖面被一块落石砸出层层波纹，水下的水草被搅得东倒西歪
scene: 深夜的居民楼里，楼上的电钻声断断续续响了两个小时，楼下的老人终于上楼敲门。The drilling upstairs caused a serious disturbance that brought the neighbours to the door.
sceneCN: 这里 disturbance 指「扰人安宁的行为」（第 1 个义项：打断他人平静与正常秩序的事件）；句意：楼上的电钻造成严重扰民，把邻居引到了门口。图中可辨识物件：居民楼走廊、电钻、敲门的手、墙上的挂钟。

pos.zh: 干扰；扰动；扰乱；骚乱（可数或不可数，复数为 disturbances）

senses.title: Breaking someone's peace
senses.titleCN: 扰人安宁：打断他人的平静
senses.definition: an act that interrupts another person's quiet or normal activity
senses.definitionCN: 打断他人安静或正常活动的行为
senses.example: The loud music at midnight was a disturbance for the whole block.
senses.exampleCN: 午夜的高声音乐扰了整条街。
senses.why: dis- here works as 'apart, in different directions' and turbare means to throw into disorder, so the act scatters a settled state.
senses.whyCN: dis- 在此表「散开、朝不同方向」，turbare 意为「搅乱」，因此这个行为把安定的状态打散。

senses.title: An ecological event that reshapes habitat
senses.titleCN: 生态扰动：重塑生境的事件
senses.definition: in ecology, an event such as fire, storm or grazing that changes the structure of an habitat
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中指火灾、风暴、放牧等改变生境结构的事件
senses.example: A single windstorm was the disturbance that opened the forest floor to light.
senses.exampleCN: 一场风灾就是那次让林下见到阳光的扰动。
senses.why: ecology needed a neutral word for any event that breaks the existing order, so the everyday sense was extended.
senses.whyCN: 生态学需要一个中性词来指任何打破既有秩序的事件，于是日常义被扩展过去。

senses.title: A disruption of normal function
senses.titleCN: 功能紊乱：正常运作被打断
senses.definition: an interruption of a bodily or mechanical function
senses.definitionCN: 身体或机械功能的正常运作被打断
senses.example: Long shift work causes a disturbance of the sleep cycle.
senses.exampleCN: 长期轮班工作会造成睡眠周期的紊乱。
senses.why: the same scattering applies to internal rhythms: what ran evenly now runs out of step.
senses.whyCN: 同一种「打散」也适用于内部节律：原本均匀运转的东西现在乱了拍子。

senses.title: Public disorder or a riot
senses.titleCN: 骚乱：公共秩序的失控
senses.definition: a public outbreak of disorder, often involving a crowd
senses.definitionCN: 公共秩序失控的事件，常涉及人群聚集
senses.example: Troops were called in after a disturbance broke out in the market.
senses.exampleCN: 市场爆发骚乱后，军队被调来。
senses.why: when many people are thrown out of order at once, the individual interruption becomes a collective event.
senses.whyCN: 当许多人同时被抛离秩序，个体的打扰就变成集体事件。

senses.title: A deviation from equilibrium
senses.titleCN: 偏离平衡：系统上的扰动
senses.definition: a small push that moves a system away from its equilibrium state
senses.definitionCN: 使系统离开平衡态的小幅推动
senses.example: Engineers applied a small disturbance to test the control system.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师施加一个小扰动来测试控制系统。
senses.why: physics formalised the everyday word: any nudge that displaces a system counts, however small.
senses.whyCN: 物理学把这个日常词形式化：任何使系统偏离的推动都算，无论多小。

senses.title: A nuisance in law
senses.titleCN: 法律上的妨害安宁
senses.definition: in law, an interference with another person's quiet enjoyment of property
senses.definitionCN: 法律上对他人安静享用其财产权的妨害
senses.example: The factory was sued for disturbance caused by night-time noise.
senses.exampleCN: 这家工厂因夜间噪声造成的妨害被起诉。
senses.why: legal usage fixes the loose everyday sense into a claimable harm with a measurable effect.
senses.whyCN: 法律用法把松散的日常义固定为可主张、可衡量的损害。

senses.title: A sudden shift in community structure
senses.titleCN: 群落突变：组成与结构骤变
senses.definition: a change that alters the species composition or physical structure of a community
senses.definitionCN: 改变群落物种组成或物理结构的变动
senses.example: The disturbance removed the dominant shrub and let grasses invade.
senses.exampleCN: 这次扰动除去了优势灌木，让草本入侵。
senses.why: the event matters less than its result: what was dominant loses its place, and the whole assembly reorganises.
senses.whyCN: 事件本身不如其结果重要：原来的优势者失去位置，整个组合重新编排。

senses.title: Inner unease in literary use
senses.titleCN: 心绪不宁：内在的不安
senses.definition: a state of mental or emotional unsettledness
senses.definitionCN: 精神或情绪上不安定的状态
senses.example: A strange disturbance in her chest kept her from sleeping.
senses.exampleCN: 胸口一种莫名的扰动让她睡不着。
senses.why: the outer scattering is turned inward, so the word can name a mind that will not stay still.
senses.whyCN: 外在的打散转向内部，于是这个词能指一个静不下来的心。

intro.en: Disturbance comes through Old French from Latin disturbare 'to throw into disorder', built on dis- and turbare 'to disturb', itself from turba 'turmoil, crowd'. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: disturbance 经古法语出自拉丁 disturbare「搅乱」，由 dis- 与 turbare「搅动」构成，后者源自 turba「骚动、人群」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Turba named a crowd or a turmoil. Its further origin is uncertain; any older form cited for it is a reconstruction.
items.cn: turba 指人群或骚动；其更早来源不确定，凡为它引出的更古形式均属重构形式。

items.en: The verb turbare meant 'to throw into confusion, to agitate', and gave English turbulent and disturb.
items.cn: 动词 turbare 意为「搅乱、使动荡」，并衍生英语 turbulent 与 disturb。

items.en: Dis- 'apart' plus turbare produced disturbare 'to scatter, to throw into disorder'.
items.cn: dis-「分开」加 turbare 构成 disturbare「打散、使混乱」。

items.en: Old French destourber carried the word north, and English took it in the fourteenth century as disturben.
items.cn: 古法语 destourber 把词带到北方，英语于 14 世纪以 disturben 形式吸收。

items.en: The noun disturbance is recorded from the fourteenth century; the ecological sense is a twentieth-century extension.
items.cn: 名词 disturbance 自 14 世纪有记录；生态义是 20 世纪的扩展。

items.en: Twentieth-century ecology made disturbance a technical term for any event that disrupts a community, with no implication of harm.
items.cn: 20 世纪生态学把 disturbance 变成术语，指任何打断群落的事件，并不含「有害」之意。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes built on the same Latin turbare; group two holds near meanings that stress a different part of the event.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁 turbare 的形近词；第二组是侧重事件不同方面的近义词。

entries.definition: To break someone's peace or to upset a process. Disturbance is the event or state that results.
entries.definitionCN: 指打扰他人安宁或扰乱某一过程；disturbance 是它造成的事件或状态。

entries.definition: Describing someone or something already affected; it looks at the receiver, not the event.
entries.definitionCN: 形容已受影响的人或物；着眼点在承受者，而不在事件。

entries.definition: From the same turbare, but it names ongoing swirling motion, as in turbulent water or times.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 turbare，但指持续翻滚的流动，如湍流或动荡的时代。

entries.definition: The state of swirling disorder, especially in air or water. It is a condition, not a single event.
entries.definitionCN: 指翻腾的紊乱状态，尤指气流或水流；是一种状态，不是单个事件。

entries.definition: A slight push away from a normal path, used in physics and mathematics; it is usually smaller and more precise than disturbance.
entries.definitionCN: 指使系统偏离正常轨迹的轻微推动，用于物理与数学；通常比 disturbance 更小、更精确。

entries.definition: A temporary stop in speech, work or supply. It marks a pause, not a reshaping of structure.
entries.definitionCN: 指话语、工作或供应的暂时中断；强调停顿，而非结构被重塑。

entries.definition: A big, often social or political, shaking up. It implies deep change, while disturbance can be minor.
entries.definitionCN: 指大规模、常为社会或政治的剧变；暗含深层改变，而 disturbance 可以是轻微的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: dis- 'apart' + turbare 'to stir up': the settled state is stirred apart.
normal.cn: dis-「分开」+ turbare「搅动」：安定的状态被搅散。

normal.en: The family runs disturb, disturbance, disturbed, disturbing, turbulent.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 disturb、disturbance、disturbed、disturbing、turbulent。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: ecological disturbance, human disturbance, cause a disturbance, disturbance regime.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：生态扰动、人为干扰、引起骚动、扰动格局。

normal.en: Ecology treats it as neutral: fire and storms are disturbances, not disasters.
normal.cn: 生态学把它当中性词：火灾与风暴是扰动，并不等于灾难。

normal.en: Physics pairs it with equilibrium: a small push away from rest.
normal.cn: 物理学把它与平衡配对：使其离开静止的小幅推动。

abstract.en: Picture a still pond hit by one stone: rings spread and the bottom mud lifts.
abstract.cn: 想象一块石头砸进静水：涟漪散开，底部泥被扬起。

abstract.en: Picture a neatly stacked woodpile knocked over by a passing cart.
abstract.cn: 想象码得整齐的柴堆被路过的车撞倒。

abstract.en: Picture a sleeper woken by a door slamming in the next room.
abstract.cn: 想象隔壁关门声把睡着的人惊醒。

examples.en: A hurricane is a natural disturbance that can reset forest succession.
examples.cn: 飓风是一种自然扰动，能让森林演替重新开始。

examples.en: Even low levels of human disturbance can drive nesting birds away.
examples.cn: 即使轻度的人为干扰也能把筑巢的鸟赶走。

examples.en: The patient reported a disturbance in his sense of balance.
examples.cn: 病人诉说平衡感出现了紊乱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「的士（dis）搅土（turb）→ 平静的地面被车轮搅乱」——打断秩序、搅乱生境 → 干扰、扰动

root: 拉丁 dis-「分开」+ turbare「搅动」，源自 turba「骚动、人群」（turba 更早来源不确定）→ disturbare「搅乱」；经古法语进入英语，生态学术语义为 20 世纪扩展。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something settled is stirred apart, whether that is a neighbour's quiet, a forest floor, a sleep rhythm, a crowd, an equilibrium, a legal right, a community or a mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：原本安定的东西被搅散，对象可以是邻居的安宁、林地、睡眠节律、人群、平衡态、法定权利、群落或心绪。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone dropped into still water, scattering the settled surface.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块石头砸入静水，把安定的水面打散。

branches.en: SOCIAL SURFACE: a person's peace or a crowd's order is the first thing disturbed.
branches.cn: 社会表面：最先被扰的是个人的安宁或人群的秩序。

branches.en: ECOLOGICAL RESET: fire, wind or grazing rewrites the community's structure.
branches.cn: 生态重置：火、风或放牧改写群落结构。

branches.en: INNER RHYTHM: a body function or a mind falls out of step.
branches.cn: 内在节律：身体功能或心绪乱了拍子。

branches.en: EQUILIBRIUM PUSH: in physics even a tiny nudge counts as a disturbance.
branches.cn: 平衡推动：在物理中，哪怕极小的推动也算扰动。

branches.en: LEGAL CLAIM: the everyday nuisance becomes a harm that can be sued for.
branches.cn: 法律主张：日常的妨害变成可诉的损害。

intro.en: The noun is a Latin verb stem with the noun ending -ance; the prefix dis- keeps its older sense of 'apart'.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁动词词干加名词词尾 -ance；前缀 dis- 保留较古的「分开」义。

latinIntro.en: Latin turbare yields disturb, disturbance, turbulent, turbulence and perturb; turba itself gives the rare adjective turbid.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 turbare 衍生 disturb、disturbance、turbulent、turbulence 与 perturb；turba 本身还给出罕用的形容词 turbid。

items.meaning: the state or event of being thrown into disorder
items.example: The survey recorded every disturbance in the plot.
items.exampleCN: 调查记录了样地里的每一次扰动。

items.example: Do not disturb the nesting birds.
items.exampleCN: 不要打扰筑巢的鸟。

items.example: The disturbed soil sprouted weeds first.
items.exampleCN: 受扰的土壤先长出了杂草。

items.example: The survey found a disturbing decline in insects.
items.exampleCN: 调查发现昆虫数量下降，令人不安。

items.example: The core sample came from an undisturbed layer.
items.exampleCN: 这份岩芯取自未受扰动的层位。

items.example: Turbulent air shook the aircraft.
items.exampleCN: 湍流空气使飞机颠簸。

items.example: The aircraft hit turbulence over the mountains.
items.exampleCN: 飞机在山地上空遇到湍流。

items.meaning: to disturb greatly; to displace slightly
items.example: The moon perturbs the planet's orbit.
items.exampleCN: 月球使这颗行星的轨道发生偏离。

definition_zh: 扰动格局；某一地区长期重复发生的扰动类型、频率、强度与规模的总模式
definition_en: the long-term pattern of disturbance types, frequencies, intensities and extents that recur in a given area
core_image: 一条画着年轮的横向时间带，带上分布着大小不一的火苗、风符号与洪水记号，像一串有节律的鼓点
scene: 一片松林的横截面上画满历年火疤，护林员量出每隔十二三年就有一道。In these pine woods the disturbance regime of frequent low fires keeps the canopy open and the understory rich.
sceneCN: 这里 disturbance regime 指「扰动格局」（第 1 个义项：一个地区扰动类型、频率与强度的长期重复模式）；句意：在这片松林里，频繁低强度火灾的扰动格局使林冠保持开阔、林下保持丰富。图中可辨识物件：树轮截面、火疤年轮、测尺、松林剖面。

pos.zh: 扰动格局；扰动体系（可数，复数为 disturbance regimes）

senses.title: The recurring pattern of disturbances in one place
senses.titleCN: 长期重复：一个地区扰动的固定模式
senses.definition: the recurring combination of disturbance types that characterises a given area over decades
senses.definitionCN: 在数十年尺度上，某一地区反复出现的扰动类型组合
senses.example: The disturbance regime of the delta includes floods, storms and grazing.
senses.exampleCN: 这片三角洲的扰动格局包括洪水、风暴与放牧。
senses.why: regime names a settled order of rule, so joining it to disturbance turns scattered events into a predictable pattern.
senses.whyCN: regime 指一种稳定的统治秩序，把它与 disturbance 并置，就把零散事件变成可预期的模式。

senses.title: Frequency and return interval
senses.titleCN: 频率与重现间隔：多久来一次
senses.definition: the rate at which disturbances recur, usually given as a return interval
senses.definitionCN: 扰动重复发生的速率，通常用重现间隔表示
senses.example: A return interval of forty years defines this forest's fire regime.
senses.exampleCN: 四十年一轮的重现间隔界定了这片森林的火格局。
senses.why: the pattern is measurable once events are counted, and frequency is the first number ecologists record.
senses.whyCN: 一旦事件被计数，模式就可测量，而频率是生态学家记录的第一个数字。

senses.title: Intensity and severity profile
senses.titleCN: 强度剖面：每次来得多重
senses.definition: the typical intensity of disturbances, from low ground fires to stand-replacing events
senses.definitionCN: 扰动通常达到的强度，从地表低强度火到可替换整片林分的重扰动
senses.example: The same frequency can hide two very different disturbance regimes.
senses.exampleCN: 同样的频率可以掩盖两种截然不同的扰动格局。
senses.why: frequency alone does not describe a pattern, so severity is added as the second axis of the regime.
senses.whyCN: 仅凭频率无法描述模式，于是烈度被作为格局的第二个轴补上。

senses.title: Spatial extent and patch size
senses.titleCN: 空间范围：扰动波及多大一片
senses.definition: the typical area affected by a disturbance and the size of the patches it leaves
senses.definitionCN: 一次扰动通常波及的面积，以及它留下的斑块大小
senses.example: Small patchiness is part of this woodland's disturbance regime.
senses.exampleCN: 小尺度斑块化是这片林地的扰动格局的一部分。
senses.why: a regime also describes where events stop, so extent completes the three-dimensional picture of frequency, severity and area.
senses.whyCN: 格局还要说明事件在哪里停下，因此空间范围补全了频率、烈度与面积的三维图景。

senses.title: Fire regime as the model case
senses.titleCN: 火格局：最常被研究的特例
senses.definition: the specific disturbance regime formed by the history of fires in a landscape
senses.definitionCN: 由一处景观的火历史所形成的具体扰动格局
senses.example: Fire suppression changed the fire regime of the whole plateau.
senses.exampleCN: 灭火政策改变了整个高原的火格局。
senses.why: fire leaves readable scars in tree rings, so it became the best documented case and gave the term its standard example.
senses.whyCN: 火在年轮上留下可读的疤痕，因此成为记录最完整的案例，也为这个术语提供了标准范例。

senses.title: The historical baseline
senses.titleCN: 历史基线：人为干预之前的格局
senses.definition: the regime that prevailed before industrial or agricultural modification, used as a reference
senses.definitionCN: 在工业或农业改造之前占主导、可作参照的格局
senses.example: Managers compared the present pattern with the historical disturbance regime.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者把当前模式与历史扰动格局作比较。
senses.why: once people alter a landscape, the pre-existing pattern becomes a baseline against which change is judged.
senses.whyCN: 一旦人类改造景观，原先的模式就成了衡量变化的基线。

senses.title: A human-altered regime or regime shift
senses.titleCN: 人为改变与格局跃变
senses.definition: a disturbance pattern changed by human action, or a switch from one stable pattern to another
senses.definitionCN: 因人类活动而改变的扰动模式，或从一种稳定模式切换到另一种
senses.example: Livestock grazing pushed the grassland into a new disturbance regime.
senses.exampleCN: 放牧把这片草地推入一个新的扰动格局。
senses.why: a regime can be replaced rather than merely modified, and the word shift marks that replacement.
senses.whyCN: 格局可以被替换而不只是被修改，shift 一词标记的正是这种替换。

senses.title: A management reference frame
senses.titleCN: 管理参照系：修复目标的尺度
senses.definition: the pattern that restoration or land management aims to maintain or reinstate
senses.definitionCN: 修复或土地管理所力求维持或恢复的那种模式
senses.example: The plan set a target disturbance regime for the reserve.
senses.exampleCN: 该方案为保护区设定了一个目标扰动格局。
senses.why: in applied ecology the term stops describing and starts prescribing: the regime becomes a goal.
senses.whyCN: 在应用生态学中，这个术语从描述转为规定：格局本身成了目标。

intro.en: The phrase joins disturbance, from Latin disturbare 'to throw into disorder', to regime, from Latin regimen 'rule, guidance'. The ecological compound is a twentieth-century formation, and the dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把出自拉丁 disturbare「搅乱」的 disturbance 与出自拉丁 regimen「统治、指导」的 regime 组合起来；生态学的这一复合术语形成于 20 世纪，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Turbare 'to stir up' and its noun turba 'crowd, turmoil' supplied disturb and disturbance; the deeper origin of turba is uncertain.
items.cn: turbare「搅动」及其名词 turba「人群、骚动」给出 disturb 与 disturbance；turba 的更早来源不确定。

items.en: Regimen meant 'rule, guidance, government', from regere 'to rule, keep straight'; it named both a political order and a rule of life.
items.cn: regimen 意为「统治、指导、治理」，出自 regere「统治、使笔直」，既指政治秩序，也指生活规则。

items.en: French régime carried the political sense into English in the fifteenth century, where it settled as 'a system of rule'.
items.cn: 法语 régime 于 15 世纪把政治义带入英语，固定为「统治体制」。

items.en: Disturbance is recorded in English from the fourteenth century, at first as a term for civil and personal disorder.
items.cn: disturbance 自 14 世纪见于英语，最初指公共与个人的秩序紊乱。

items.en: Mid-twentieth-century ecology generalised regime to any recurring environmental pattern; fire ecology then fixed disturbance regime as a compound.
items.cn: 20 世纪中叶的生态学把 regime 泛化为任何重复的环境模式；火生态学随后把 disturbance regime 固定为复合术语。

items.en: The exact first use of the compound is not recorded; the 1960s and 1970s are the usual attribution, and any earlier claim is uncertain.
items.cn: 这一复合词的确切首用无记录；通常归于 20 世纪 60 至 70 年代，更早的说法均不确定。

note.en: Group one holds the parts and near neighbours of the same Latin stock; group two holds ecological terms that describe a pattern from another angle.
note.cn: 第一组是同一拉丁词源的组成部分与近邻词；第二组是从另一角度描述模式的相关生态术语。

entries.definition: A single disruptive event. The regime is the rule that those events follow over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指单次搅乱事件；格局是这些事件在时间上遵循的规律。

entries.definition: A system or settled order. On its own it says nothing about disturbance.
entries.definitionCN: 指体制或稳定秩序；单独使用时与扰动无关。

entries.tag: a rule of life, not ecology
entries.definition: A prescribed course of diet, exercise or treatment. It shares the root but belongs to medicine, not landscape ecology.
entries.definitionCN: 指规定的饮食、锻炼或疗程；同词根，但属医学而非景观生态学。

entries.definition: From the same regere, but it names an act of controlling, not a recurring natural pattern.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 regere，但指控制行为，而非重复出现的自然模式。

entries.definition: Only how often disturbances occur. The regime adds type, severity and extent.
entries.definitionCN: 只指扰动发生的频繁程度；格局还包含类型、烈度与范围。

entries.definition: The disturbance regime produced by fires alone; it is a subset of the broader term.
entries.definitionCN: 仅由火灾形成的扰动格局，是更广义术语的一个子集。

entries.definition: The sequence of communities that follows a disturbance. The regime describes the disturbance; succession describes the response.
entries.definitionCN: 指扰动之后群落依次更替的过程；格局描述扰动，演替描述响应。

entries.definition: A single dated occurrence, such as one fire. A regime is the statistical shape of many such events.
entries.definitionCN: 指一次有日期的发生，如一场火；格局是许多此类事件的统计形态。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: disturbance 'the event' + regime 'the settled order': the order that events keep.
normal.cn: disturbance「事件」+ regime「稳定秩序」：事件所遵循的秩序。

normal.en: The family runs disturbance, disturb, regime, regimen, regulate, regulation.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 disturbance、disturb、regime、regimen、regulate、regulation。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: fire regime, historical regime, altered regime, regime shift.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：火格局、历史格局、被改变的格局、格局跃变。

normal.en: Fire is the model case because scars in tree rings make frequency readable.
normal.cn: 火是标准案例，因为年轮上的疤痕使频率可读。

normal.en: Managers use the term prescriptively: a target regime is a restoration goal.
normal.cn: 管理者把这个术语用作规定：目标格局就是修复目标。

abstract.en: Picture a drumbeat: not one strike but a rhythm of loud and soft beats.
abstract.cn: 想象一段鼓点：不是单独一击，而是强弱相间的节律。

abstract.en: Picture a calendar with fire marks scattered at a fairly steady spacing.
abstract.cn: 想象一本日历上，火痕以大致均匀的间隔散布。

abstract.en: Picture a thermostat that keeps a room within a set band rather than at one fixed point.
abstract.cn: 想象一个恒温器，让房间停在某个区间，而不是某一定点。

examples.en: Restoring the historical disturbance regime may require controlled burns.
examples.cn: 恢复历史扰动格局可能需要计划烧除。

examples.en: Grazing and drought together created a disturbance regime unlike any in the record.
examples.cn: 放牧与干旱共同造成了一种记录中从未出现的扰动格局。

examples.en: A change in the disturbance regime favoured shrubs over grasses.
examples.cn: 扰动格局的改变使灌木比草本更占优势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「扰动 + 制度」——把零散的天灾人祸排成一张有节律的值班表 → 扰动格局

root: 拉丁 disturbare「搅乱」（dis- + turbare，源自 turba「人群、骚动」）+ 拉丁 regimen「统治、指导」（源自 regere「统治、使笔直」）；生态学复合术语形成于 20 世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses turn a scatter of events into a describable order: type, frequency, severity, extent, the fire case, the historical baseline, human change and the management target.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把零散事件变成可描述的顺序：类型、频率、烈度、范围、火的特例、历史基线、人为改变与管理目标。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rhythm of shocks recorded along a timeline, each with its own size and reach.
core.cn: 核心意象：沿时间轴记录的一串冲击节律，每一次各有大小与波及范围。

branches.en: PATTERN AND ITS MODEL: the general recurring order, with fire as the best documented instance.
branches.cn: 模式与其范例：一般性的重复秩序，火是记录最完整的实例。

branches.en: THREE AXES: frequency, severity and extent are the measurements that make a regime describable.
branches.cn: 三条轴：频率、烈度与范围，是使格局可描述的三项测量。

branches.en: BASELINE: the pattern before human modification becomes the reference point.
branches.cn: 基线：人类改造之前的模式成为参照点。

branches.en: REPLACEMENT: human action can push a landscape into a different regime.
branches.cn: 替换：人类活动可把景观推入另一种格局。

branches.en: TARGET: in management the pattern turns from description into prescription.
branches.cn: 目标：在管理中，格局从描述转为规定。

intro.en: The compound is two Latin-derived nouns; one carries the -ance noun ending, the other the -men ending of a Latin noun of means or rule.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由两个拉丁来源名词构成：一个带 -ance 名词词尾，另一个带拉丁表示手段或规则的名词词尾 -men。

latinIntro.en: Latin turbare gives disturb, disturbance, turbulent and perturb; Latin regere gives regime, regimen, regulate, regular and regulation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 turbare 衍生 disturb、disturbance、turbulent 与 perturb；拉丁 regere 衍生 regime、regimen、regulate、regular 与 regulation。

items.meaning: the settled order followed by disruptive events
items.meaningCN: 搅乱事件所遵循的稳定秩序
items.example: The reserve keeps a natural disturbance regime.
items.exampleCN: 保护区维持着自然扰动格局。

items.example: Each disturbance opens a gap in the canopy.
items.exampleCN: 每次扰动都在林冠上开出一个缺口。

items.meaning: a system of rule; a recurring pattern
items.meaningCN: 统治体制；重复出现的模式
items.example: The river's flood regime has shifted.
items.exampleCN: 这条河的洪水格局已经改变。

items.meaning: a rule of life or treatment
items.example: The clinic prescribed a strict regimen.
items.exampleCN: 诊所规定了严格的疗程。

items.example: Fire helps regulate the build-up of fuel.
items.exampleCN: 火有助于调节可燃物的积累。

items.example: New regulations limited logging in the reserve.
items.exampleCN: 新规定限制了保护区内的采伐。

items.example: The fires were regular in their return.
items.exampleCN: 这些火灾的重现间隔很均匀。

items.example: Deregulation of the water market followed.
items.exampleCN: 随后水市场放松了管制。

definition_zh: 恢复；康复；找回；回收；（生态）恢复
definition_en: the process of returning to a former condition, of getting something back, or of regaining health
core_image: 一只被浪打翻的小船被潮水慢慢扶正，船底重新露出水面
scene: 台风过后渔船都进了港，两个月后新的防波堤合拢，码头重新开始卸货。Two months after the typhoon the harbour had made a full recovery and the boats were landing fish again.
sceneCN: 这里 recovery 指「（受灾后）恢复原状」（第 2 个义项：回到灾前的结构与功能状态）；句意：台风过后两个月，港口完全恢复，渔船又能卸货了。图中可辨识物件：合拢的防波堤、卸货的渔船、码头吊机、水位标尺。

pos.zh: 恢复；康复；找回；回收（可数或不可数，复数为 recoveries）

senses.title: Return to health
senses.titleCN: 康复：病后回到健康
senses.definition: the process of becoming healthy again after illness or injury
senses.definitionCN: 患病或受伤之后重新变得健康的过程
senses.example: Her recovery from the fever took three weeks.
senses.exampleCN: 她退烧后的康复用了三周。
senses.why: re- marks 'back' and the Latin root names getting something again, so health is pictured as something regained.
senses.whyCN: re- 表「回到」，拉丁词根意为「重新取得」，因此健康被想象成重新拿回来的东西。

senses.title: Return to a former condition
senses.titleCN: 复原：回到灾前的状态
senses.definition: the return of a place, system or economy to its condition before a shock
senses.definitionCN: 地点、系统或经济在受冲击后回到此前状态
senses.example: The harbour made a full recovery within two months.
senses.exampleCN: 港口在两个月内完全恢复。
senses.why: the image is extended from a body to any system that can be brought back to its earlier state.
senses.whyCN: 这个意象从身体扩展到任何能被带回先前状态的系统。

senses.title: Getting something back
senses.titleCN: 找回：把失去的东西拿回来
senses.definition: the act of regaining possession of something lost or taken
senses.definitionCN: 重新取得丢失或被拿走之物的行为
senses.example: The recovery of the stolen instruments took a year.
senses.exampleCN: 找回被盗的乐器花了一年。
senses.why: this is the most literal branch: a thing leaves your hands and then comes back to them.
senses.whyCN: 这是最字面的一支：东西离开你的手，然后又回到手中。

senses.title: Economic upturn
senses.titleCN: 经济复苏：产出与就业回升
senses.definition: the phase in which an economy grows again after a recession
senses.definitionCN: 经济在衰退之后重新增长的阶段
senses.example: Tourism led the recovery of the island's economy.
senses.exampleCN: 旅游业带动了该岛经济的复苏。
senses.why: economists borrowed the medical image of a patient getting well and applied it to output and jobs.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家借用了病人康复的医学意象，把它用到产出与就业上。

senses.title: Retrieval of stored data
senses.titleCN: 数据恢复：把丢失的记录取回
senses.definition: the process of retrieving data that has been damaged or deleted
senses.definitionCN: 取回已损坏或已删除的数据的过程
senses.example: Recovery of the field notes was possible after the drive failed.
senses.exampleCN: 硬盘损坏后，野外记录仍然可以恢复。
senses.why: digital loss repeats the same shape: information is mislaid and then retrieved by a procedure.
senses.whyCN: 数字丢失重复了同一形状：信息被放错地方，再通过一套程序取回。

senses.title: Extraction of useful material
senses.titleCN: 回收：从废弃物中提取资源
senses.definition: the extraction of useful materials from waste or from a mixture
senses.definitionCN: 从废弃物或混合物中提取有用物质
senses.example: Heat recovery from the kiln lowered the plant's fuel use.
senses.exampleCN: 从窑炉回收热量降低了工厂的燃料消耗。
senses.why: what would be thrown away is brought back into use, which is recovery in its material form.
senses.whyCN: 本会被丢弃的东西被带回使用，这就是物质形态的回收。

senses.title: Legal compensation
senses.titleCN: 追偿：法律上取回损失
senses.definition: in law, the obtaining of compensation or of property by legal action
senses.definitionCN: 法律上通过诉讼取得赔偿或取回财产
senses.example: The court ordered recovery of the unpaid rent.
senses.exampleCN: 法院判令追回未付租金。
senses.why: law gives the everyday 'getting back' a formal procedure and a named claimant.
senses.whyCN: 法律给日常的「取回」配上正式程序与明确的请求人。

senses.title: Ecological return toward a reference state
senses.titleCN: 生态恢复：向参照状态靠拢
senses.definition: in ecology, the return of a damaged ecosystem toward a reference condition
senses.definitionCN: 生态学中指受损生态系统向参照状态靠拢
senses.example: Recovery of the seagrass bed took a decade after the dredging stopped.
senses.exampleCN: 停止疏浚后，海草床的恢复用了十年。
senses.why: ecology specifies what 'back' means by naming a reference state measured before the damage.
senses.whyCN: 生态学通过指定受损前测得的参照状态，明确了「回到」何处。

intro.en: Recovery comes from recover plus -y; recover entered English through Old French recovrer from Latin recuperare 'to regain'. The makeup of recuperare is debated, and the dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: recovery 由 recover 加 -y 构成；recover 经古法语 recovrer 出自拉丁 recuperare「重新取得」。recuperare 的构成有争议，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Recuperare meant 'to recover, regain, restore'. The second element is usually connected with capere 'to take, grasp', but that link is debated, so the root is uncertain.
items.cn: recuperare 意为「恢复、重新取得、复原」。其后一成分通常与 capere「抓取」联系，但这一联系有争议，因此词根存疑。

items.en: Recipere 'to take back, receive' is built on the same capere; it is a near relative rather than the direct source of recover.
items.cn: recipere「取回、接受」同样基于 capere；它是近亲，而非 recover 的直接来源。

items.en: Old French recovrer carried the medical and legal senses north, and English adopted it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 recovrer 把医学与法律义带到北方，英语于 14 世纪吸收。

items.en: The abstract noun recovery is recorded by the fifteenth century; -y here forms a noun of process from the verb.
items.cn: 抽象名词 recovery 于 15 世纪有记录；这里的 -y 由动词构成表过程的名词。

items.en: Twentieth-century economics fixed 'recovery' as the phase after a recession, giving the word a technical economic sense.
items.cn: 20 世纪经济学把 recovery 固定为衰退之后的阶段，使其获得经济学术语义。

items.en: Later twentieth-century ecology and computing each added a sense: return to a reference state, and retrieval of damaged data.
items.cn: 20 世纪后期的生态学与计算机各自增添一义：回到参照状态，以及取回损坏的数据。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes that share the letters but not always the root; group two holds near meanings distinguished by what is regained.
note.cn: 第一组是字形相近、但并非总是同源的词；第二组是近义词，区别在于「取回什么」。

entries.definition: To get well or get something back. Recovery is the process or the instance of it.
entries.definitionCN: 指康复或取回；recovery 是这一过程或其中一次实例。

entries.definition: To put a new cover on something, from cover with the prefix re- 'again'. It has nothing to do with recuperation.
entries.definitionCN: 指给某物换新罩面，由 cover 加 re-「再一次」构成，与康复无关。

entries.definition: To regain health or strength. It is close to the medical branch of recovery but cannot mean 'get an object back'.
entries.definitionCN: 指恢复健康或体力，接近 recovery 的医学义，但不能表示「取回物品」。

entries.definition: The process of convalescence. Its scope is narrower than recovery, which covers economies and data too.
entries.definitionCN: 指休养康复的过程；范围比 recovery 窄，后者还覆盖经济与数据。

entries.definition: Putting something back into a chosen earlier condition by active work. Recovery can happen on its own.
entries.definitionCN: 通过主动工作把某物放回选定的旧状态；recovery 可以是自行发生的。

entries.definition: A quick bounce back after a low point, often in prices or mood. It stresses speed rather than completeness.
entries.definitionCN: 指跌到低点后的快速回弹，常用于价格或情绪；强调速度而非彻底。

entries.definition: Bringing a person or a damaged land back to useful function, often with training or treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过训练或治理使人或受损土地恢复可用功能。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'back' + capere 'to take': to take back what was lost.
normal.cn: re-「回」+ capere「拿」：把失去的东西拿回来。

normal.en: The family runs recover, recovery, recoverable, unrecoverable, recuperate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 recover、recovery、recoverable、unrecoverable、recuperate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: full recovery, economic recovery, data recovery, disaster recovery.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：完全恢复、经济复苏、数据恢复、灾后恢复。

normal.en: Ecology adds a reference state; the word then means return to a measured baseline.
normal.cn: 生态学加进参照状态；此时这个词指回到已测量的基线。

normal.en: Note the minimal pair re-cover 'put a new cover on', stressed on cover.
normal.cn: 注意最小对立组 re-cover「换新罩面」，重音落在 cover 上。

abstract.en: Picture a capsized boat righting itself as the tide turns.
abstract.cn: 想象一只翻船随着潮水转向自行扶正。

abstract.en: Picture a patient's chart turning from a falling line to a rising one.
abstract.cn: 想象病人的图表从下行线转为上行线。

abstract.en: Picture a lost key found again in the coat you wore last winter.
abstract.cn: 想象丢失的钥匙在去年冬天那件外套里又被找到。

examples.en: After the drought, the recovery of the grassland depended on autumn rain.
examples.cn: 干旱之后，这片草地的恢复取决于秋雨。

examples.en: The hospital reported a full recovery in nine out of ten cases.
examples.cn: 医院报告十例中有九例完全康复。

examples.en: Recovery of the damaged files took the technicians two days.
examples.cn: 技术人员花了两天恢复损坏的文件。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞（re）靠（cover）里」——靠一层覆盖把翻倒的东西盖回原位 → 恢复、康复

root: 拉丁 recuperare「重新取得、恢复」（第二成分常与 capere「抓取」联系，但此联系有争议，故词根存疑）；经古法语 recovrer 进入英语，加 -y 构成名词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: something is lost or knocked down, and then comes back, whether it is health, a system, a possession, an economy, data, material, a legal loss or an ecosystem.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：某物丢失或被击倒，随后又回来；对象可以是健康、系统、财物、经济、数据、材料、法律损失或生态系统。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a capsized boat slowly righting itself until it floats level again.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只翻倒的船慢慢扶正，重新平浮在水面。

branches.en: BODY AND PLACE: health or a whole settlement comes back to its earlier state.
branches.cn: 身体与地点：健康或整个聚落回到先前的状态。

branches.en: POSSESSION: what was taken is recovered, by hand or by court order.
branches.cn: 所有物：被拿走的东西靠双手或法院命令取回。

branches.en: ECONOMY: output and jobs climb back after a recession.
branches.cn: 经济：衰退之后产出与就业回升。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND DATA: lost records are retrieved and waste is put back to use.
branches.cn: 数据与材料：丢失的记录被取回，废弃物被重新利用。

branches.en: ECOSYSTEM: the return is judged against a recorded reference state.
branches.cn: 生态系统：恢复以有记录的参照状态为衡量标准。

intro.en: The noun is a verb plus -y; the verb itself carries the Latin prefix re- and a debated second element.
intro.cn: 这个名词由动词加 -y 构成；动词本身带拉丁前缀 re- 与一个尚有争议的第二成分。

latinIntro.en: Latin recuperare yields recover, recovery, recoverable and recuperate; the related capere yields capture, captive and receive.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 recuperare 衍生 recover、recovery、recoverable 与 recuperate；相关的 capere 衍生 capture、captive 与 receive。

items.example: The recovery of the marsh took fifteen years.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽的恢复用了十五年。

items.meaning: to get back; to become well
items.example: The reef began to recover once fishing stopped.
items.exampleCN: 停止捕捞后珊瑚礁开始恢复。

items.example: Most of the metal is recoverable from the ash.
items.exampleCN: 灰中的大部分金属可以回收。

items.example: The oldest files were unrecoverable.
items.exampleCN: 最旧的文件已无法恢复。

items.example: The recoverer of the wreck filed a claim.
items.exampleCN: 沉船的打捞者提交了申请。

items.example: He recuperated in a quiet village.
items.exampleCN: 他在一个安静的村子休养。

items.example: Recuperation after surgery takes months.
items.exampleCN: 手术后的康复需要数月。

items.example: The climate has a recuperative effect.
items.exampleCN: 这种气候有助康复。

definition_zh: 再生；更新；（森林）天然更新；复兴
definition_en: the regrowth of lost tissue or vegetation, and more broadly the renewal of a system or a place
core_image: 被截断的蚯蚓尾端一点点长出新的体节，断口边缘先是一层薄薄的新肉
scene: 砍伐后的山坡先铺满苔藓与草本，随后成片冒起桦树苗，十年后又是一片幼林。On the cleared slope, natural regeneration began with moss and grass and ended with a young birch wood.
sceneCN: 这里 regeneration 指「植被天然更新」（第 2 个义项：森林在受扰后自行重新长出新一代林木）；句意：在清伐后的坡地上，天然更新从苔藓与草本开始，最后长成一片幼桦林。图中可辨识物件：苔藓层、草本、桦树苗、幼林轮廓。

pos.zh: 再生；更新；复兴（可数或不可数，复数为 regenerations）

senses.title: Biological regrowth of lost tissue
senses.titleCN: 组织再生：长回失去的部分
senses.definition: the regrowth of cells, tissue or a body part that has been lost or damaged
senses.definitionCN: 细胞、组织或身体部件在失去或受损后重新长出
senses.example: Lizard tail regeneration takes several months.
senses.exampleCN: 蜥蜴尾巴的再生需要数月。
senses.why: re- 'again' plus generare 'to beget' names a second birth of the same part.
senses.whyCN: re-「再一次」加 generare「生育」，指同一部位获得第二次生长。

senses.title: Renewal of forest or vegetation
senses.titleCN: 植被更新：新一代林木长起
senses.definition: the establishment of a new generation of trees or plants after harvesting or disturbance
senses.definitionCN: 在采伐或扰动之后新一代树木或植物建立起来
senses.example: Natural regeneration depends on seed trees left standing.
senses.exampleCN: 天然更新依赖留存的母树。
senses.why: forestry applies the same 'new generation' idea to a stand rather than to a single tissue.
senses.whyCN: 林学把同一个「新一代」的概念从单个组织扩展到整片林分。

senses.title: Spiritual rebirth
senses.titleCN: 灵魂重生：宗教意义上的更新
senses.definition: a renewal of the soul or of a person's moral life, especially in Christian usage
senses.definitionCN: 灵魂或道德生活的更新，尤见于基督教用语
senses.example: The sermon described baptism as a regeneration of the spirit.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇讲道把洗礼描述为灵魂的重生。
senses.why: the earliest English sense is theological: a new life given from outside the person.
senses.whyCN: 英语最早的含义是神学的：从人之外赐予的新生命。

senses.title: Urban or economic renewal
senses.titleCN: 城市更新：旧区的复苏
senses.definition: the revival of a declining district or economy through investment and rebuilding
senses.definitionCN: 通过投资与重建使衰退城区或经济复苏
senses.example: The docklands regeneration brought new housing and jobs.
senses.exampleCN: 码头区的更新带来了新住房与就业。
senses.why: a district is treated as a body that can grow a new layer over its old fabric.
senses.whyCN: 城区被当成一个身体，能在旧结构上长出新的一层。

senses.title: Restoring a system's capacity
senses.titleCN: 系统能力恢复：功能重新运转
senses.definition: the restoration of a system's ability to function after decline or damage
senses.definitionCN: 系统在衰退或受损后恢复运作能力
senses.example: The regeneration of the soil's microbial community took years.
senses.exampleCN: 土壤微生物群落的恢复花了数年。
senses.why: the sense focuses on capacity rather than on the visible parts, so it applies to soil, reefs or institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项着眼能力而非可见部件，因此可用于土壤、礁体或机构。

senses.title: Rebuilding a population
senses.titleCN: 种群重建：个体数量回升
senses.definition: the recovery of a population through reproduction after a decline
senses.definitionCN: 种群在数量下降后通过繁殖回升
senses.example: Wolf regeneration in the park followed a ban on hunting.
senses.exampleCN: 禁猎之后，公园里的狼群得以重建。
senses.why: when the unit is a breeding group rather than a body part, 'new generation' becomes population growth.
senses.whyCN: 当单位是繁殖群体而非身体部件时，「新一代」就变成种群增长。

senses.title: Industrial regeneration of materials
senses.titleCN: 工业再生：材料与介质复原
senses.definition: the restoration of a spent material or medium so that it can be used again
senses.definitionCN: 使用过的材料或介质恢复可用状态
senses.example: Catalyst regeneration cut the refinery's costs.
senses.exampleCN: 催化剂再生降低了炼厂成本。
senses.why: industry reuses the biological word for a technical second life of a material.
senses.whyCN: 工业借用了生物学的词，指材料在技术上获得的第二次寿命。

senses.title: Literary renewal of memory or ideas
senses.titleCN: 文学义：记忆与观念的复苏
senses.definition: the revival of a memory, idea or tradition that had faded
senses.definitionCN: 已淡去的记忆、观念或传统重新活跃
senses.example: The festival led to a regeneration of the old dialect.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节日带来了古老方言的复苏。
senses.why: the least physical branch: what returns is not tissue but a pattern of thought or speech.
senses.whyCN: 最不具实体的一支：回来的不是组织，而是一套思想或言语模式。

intro.en: Regeneration comes from Latin regeneratio, built on regenerare 'to bring forth again', itself re- plus generare 'to beget' from genus 'birth, race'. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: regeneration 出自拉丁 regeneratio，基于 regenerare「再次产生」，后者由 re- 加 generare「生育」构成，而 generare 源自 genus「出生、族类」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Genus meant 'birth, origin, race, kind'; its stem gener- carries the idea of a line coming into being.
items.cn: genus 意为「出生、来源、族类、种类」；其词干 gener- 承载「一条血脉产生出来」的意思。

items.en: Generare 'to beget, produce' gave English generate and generation; it names bringing a new instance into existence.
items.cn: generare「生育、产生」衍生英语 generate 与 generation；它指使一个新个体进入存在。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus generare produced regenerare 'to bring forth again', used of both living things and spiritual renewal.
items.cn: re-「再一次」加 generare 构成 regenerare「再次产生」，既用于生物，也用于精神更新。

items.en: Regeneration became a technical term in early Christian Latin for the new life of baptism, and this sense came into English first.
items.cn: regeneration 在早期基督教拉丁语中成为洗礼新生的术语，这一含义最先进入英语。

items.en: English adopted regeneration in the fourteenth century with the theological sense; the biological sense is recorded later.
items.cn: 英语于 14 世纪吸收 regeneration，先取神学义；生物学的含义记录得更晚。

items.en: Experimental work on hydra and planarians in the eighteenth century, and later cell biology, fixed the modern tissue sense.
items.cn: 18 世纪对水螅与涡虫的实验，以及后来的细胞生物学，确定了现代的组织再生义。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same generare family; group two holds near meanings that differ in what is renewed.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 generare 词族的形近词；第二组是近义词，区别在于「更新的是什么」。

entries.definition: To grow again or renew. Regeneration is the process or result of that verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指重新长出或更新；regeneration 是该动词的过程或结果。

entries.definition: A single stage in a family line or a single act of producing. Without re- it lacks the idea of return.
entries.definitionCN: 指家族中的一代或一次产生行为；没有 re- 就不含「返回」之意。

entries.definition: Decline from a better to a worse state, built with de- 'down'. It is the mirror image of regeneration.
entries.definitionCN: 指由较好状态向较差状态衰退，由 de-「向下」构成，是 regeneration 的反面。

entries.definition: Describing the capacity to regrow, as in regenerative medicine. It modifies a noun rather than naming the process.
entries.definitionCN: 形容具有再生能力，如再生医学；它修饰名词，而不直接命名过程。

entries.definition: Active work that returns a site to a chosen earlier condition; regeneration can be unassisted.
entries.definitionCN: 通过主动工作把地点恢复到选定的旧状态；再生可以是无人协助的。

entries.definition: Making something fresh or valid again, used for licences, vows and city districts alike; it is broader and less biological.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物重新新鲜或重新有效，可用于执照、誓言与城区；范围更广，生物学色彩更弱。

entries.definition: The new growth itself, especially of plants. It names the visible result rather than the whole process.
entries.definitionCN: 指新长出的部分本身，尤指植物；命名可见结果，而非整个过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + generare 'to beget': a second birth.
normal.cn: re-「再一次」+ generare「生育」：第二次出生。

normal.en: The family runs generate, generation, regenerate, regeneration, regenerative, degenerate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 generate、generation、regenerate、regeneration、regenerative、degenerate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: tissue regeneration, forest regeneration, urban regeneration, natural regeneration.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：组织再生、森林更新、城市更新、天然更新。

normal.en: Forestry pairs it with seed trees: the parents left standing supply the next stand.
normal.cn: 林学把它与母树配对：留下的母树供给下一代林分。

normal.en: Medicine pairs it with degeneration: one grows back, the other wears down.
normal.cn: 医学把它与退变对举：一个长回来，一个磨损坏。

abstract.en: Picture a cut worm growing a new tail segment by segment.
abstract.cn: 想象一条被切断的蚯蚓一节一节长出新尾。

abstract.en: Picture a burnt hillside greening from the bottom up.
abstract.cn: 想象烧过的山坡自下而上重新变绿。

abstract.en: Picture an old factory chimney reused as a climbing wall.
abstract.cn: 想象旧厂房的烟囱被改作攀岩墙继续使用。

examples.en: The regeneration of the forest was slowed by heavy deer browsing.
examples.cn: 鹿的过度啃食拖慢了这片森林的更新。

examples.en: Stem-cell research aims at repairing organs through regeneration.
examples.cn: 干细胞研究旨在通过再生修复器官。

examples.en: Urban regeneration often displaces the residents it claims to help.
examples.cn: 城市更新常常让声称要帮助的原住民迁走。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞（re）再生（generation）」——再来一次出生 → 组织再生、植被更新

root: 拉丁 re-「再一次」+ generare「生育」，源自 genus「出生、族类」→ regenerare「再次产生」；英语先取神学义，后固定生物学与城市更新义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one movement: a part or a place that was lost or worn out produces a new version of itself, from tissue and trees to districts, systems, populations, materials and memories.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：失去或耗损的部位与地方重新长出自身的新版本，从组织、林木到城区、系统、种群、材料与记忆。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut stump pushing out a fresh green shoot from its edge.
core.cn: 核心意象：被截断的树桩从断口边缘抽出新绿。

branches.en: TISSUE: the body regrows the part it lost.
branches.cn: 组织：身体重新长出失去的部位。

branches.en: FOREST AND POPULATION: stands and breeding groups produce their next generation.
branches.cn: 森林与种群：林分与繁殖群体产生下一代。

branches.en: SPIRIT: the earliest sense, a life given again from outside.
branches.cn: 灵魂：最早的含义，由外部再次赐予的生命。

branches.en: PLACE AND SYSTEM: districts and capacities are rebuilt rather than replaced.
branches.cn: 城区与系统：被重建而非替换的是街区与能力。

branches.en: MATERIAL AND MEMORY: what was spent or faded is made usable or audible again.
branches.cn: 材料与记忆：耗尽的重新可用，淡去的重新可闻。

intro.en: The noun joins the Latin prefix re- to the verb generare and takes the noun ending -ion; the whole family turns on the stem gener-.
intro.cn: 这个名词把拉丁前缀 re- 接在动词 generare 上，并带名词词尾 -ion；整个词族都围绕词干 gener- 展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin genus and generare yield generate, generation, regenerate, regeneration, regenerative, degenerate and generic.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 genus 与 generare 衍生 generate、generation、regenerate、regeneration、regenerative、degenerate 与 generic。

items.meaning: the process of being brought forth again
items.example: Coral regeneration can take decades.
items.exampleCN: 珊瑚的再生可能需要数十年。

items.example: The shrub regenerates after fire.
items.exampleCN: 这种灌木在火后能再生。

items.example: Regenerative farming rebuilds soil carbon.
items.exampleCN: 再生农业重建土壤碳。

items.meaning: a producing; one stage of descent
items.example: Each generation of pines is cut at sixty years.
items.exampleCN: 每一代松树在六十年时被采伐。

items.meaning: to produce or bring into being
items.example: The marsh generates its own peat.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽自行生成泥炭。

items.example: The backup generator started at once.
items.exampleCN: 备用发电机立刻启动。

items.meaning: to fall from a former kind
items.example: The tissue degenerates without blood supply.
items.exampleCN: 没有血供，组织会退变。

items.example: Generic names group the species.
items.exampleCN: 属名把物种归成类。

definition_en: to grow again after being lost or damaged, or to restore something to a working state
core_image: 断枝的切口处冒出一圈浅绿色的新芽，把旧疤顶开
scene: 把剪下来的柳条插进湿土里，切口很快冒出新芽。Cut willow stems regenerate quickly when they are laid in damp soil.
sceneCN: 这里 regenerate 指「重新长出新组织」（第 1 个义项：失去或受损的部位重新长出）；句意：剪下的柳条放进湿土后很快再生出新芽。图中可辨识物件：柳条切口、新芽、湿土、水痕。

pos.zh: 再生；使恢复；重建；更新（及物或不及物）

senses.title: Regrow a lost body part
senses.titleCN: 再生身体部分：长回失去的组织
senses.definition: to grow back a part of the body that has been lost or damaged
senses.definitionCN: 重新长出已失去或受损的身体部分
senses.example: Some lizards can regenerate a lost tail.
senses.exampleCN: 有些蜥蜴能再生失去的尾巴。
senses.why: re- 'again' plus generare 'to beget' means the body gives itself a second copy of the lost part.
senses.whyCN: re-「再一次」加 generare「生育」，意思是身体为自己再造一份失去的部分。

senses.title: Grow a new plant or stand
senses.titleCN: 植物更新：从残体长成新株
senses.definition: to produce new shoots or a new generation of plants from surviving roots or seed
senses.definitionCN: 从存活的根或种子长出新的枝条或新一代植株
senses.example: The coppiced hazel regenerates from its stump.
senses.exampleCN: 矮林作业后的榛树从树桩再生。
senses.why: plants keep growing points, so cutting back is not death but the start of another generation.
senses.whyCN: 植物保留着生长点，因此被截断不是死亡，而是另一代的开始。

senses.title: Revive a declining district
senses.titleCN: 复兴街区：让旧区重新有活力
senses.definition: to improve a declining urban area through investment and new activity
senses.definitionCN: 通过投资与新活动使衰退城区重新活跃
senses.example: The city regenerated the old harbour into a market district.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市把旧港区改造成集市街区。
senses.why: the biological image is applied to a district that grows new functions on an old frame.
senses.whyCN: 生物意象被用到城区：旧框架上长出新的功能。

senses.title: Restore the vigour of a system
senses.titleCN: 系统恢复活力：使重新运转
senses.definition: to restore the activity or health of an economy, institution or system
senses.definitionCN: 使经济、机构或系统恢复活动与健康
senses.example: Cheap power helped regenerate the region's industry.
senses.exampleCN: 廉价电力帮助该地区工业重新焕发活力。
senses.why: a system that was running down is made to run again, which is the same return as in the body.
senses.whyCN: 原本走向停摆的系统重新运转，这与身体上的回归是同一回事。

senses.title: Rebuild a degraded ecosystem
senses.titleCN: 重建退化生态系统
senses.definition: to restore the structure and function of a damaged ecosystem
senses.definitionCN: 恢复受损生态系统的结构与功能
senses.example: Wetland plants regenerate the peat that fire destroyed.
senses.exampleCN: 湿地植物重建被火烧毁的泥炭。
senses.why: the verb takes an ecosystem as its object, so renewal is measured in structure and function rather than in cells.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词可以带生态系统作宾语，因此更新以结构与功能而非细胞来衡量。

senses.title: Renew a spent material
senses.titleCN: 材料再生：使旧材料可再用
senses.definition: to restore a used material or medium so that it can serve again
senses.definitionCN: 使使用过的材料或介质恢复可用
senses.example: The plant regenerates its ion-exchange resin with acid.
senses.exampleCN: 工厂用酸使离子交换树脂再生。
senses.why: industry gives a material a second working life, borrowing the biological verb for a technical cycle.
senses.whyCN: 工业让材料获得第二个使用周期，把生物学动词借到技术循环上。

senses.title: Renew spiritually or morally
senses.titleCN: 精神重生：道德与心志的更新
senses.definition: to renew a person's spirit or moral life
senses.definitionCN: 更新一个人的精神或道德生活
senses.example: The retreat was meant to regenerate the volunteers' sense of purpose.
senses.exampleCN: 这次静修意在更新志愿者的使命感。
senses.why: the oldest sense in English, where what grows again is not tissue but purpose.
senses.whyCN: 这是英语中最早的义项，重新长出的不是组织，而是目标感。

senses.title: Recreate something from records
senses.titleCN: 由记录重建：让旧状态重现
senses.definition: to rebuild a lost object or state from stored information
senses.definitionCN: 依据保存的信息重建失去的物体或状态
senses.example: The team regenerated the damaged map from survey notes.
senses.exampleCN: 团队依据测量笔记重建了损坏的地图。
senses.why: when information survives, the object can be produced again; this is regeneration without living tissue.
senses.whyCN: 当信息还在，物体就能再被造出来；这是没有活组织的再生。

intro.en: Regenerate comes from Latin regenerare 'to bring forth again', built on re- and generare 'to beget' from genus 'birth, race'. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: regenerate 出自拉丁 regenerare「再次产生」，由 re- 与 generare「生育」构成，后者源自 genus「出生、族类」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Genus named birth, origin or kind; the stem gener- carries the idea of a line being brought into being.
items.cn: genus 指出生、来源或族类；词干 gener- 承载「使一条血脉产生」的意思。

items.en: Generare meant 'to beget, produce' and is the base of generate, generation and generous.
items.cn: generare 意为「生育、产生」，是 generate、generation 与 generous 的共同基础。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus generare gave regenerare 'to bring forth again', used of plants, bodies and the soul.
items.cn: re-「再一次」加 generare 得 regenerare「再次产生」，用于植物、身体与灵魂。

items.en: The English verb is recorded in the sixteenth century, first in theological writing and then in medicine.
items.cn: 英语动词于 16 世纪有记录，先见于神学写作，后进入医学。

items.en: Eighteenth-century experiments on hydra and planarians gave the verb its modern laboratory sense.
items.cn: 18 世纪对水螅与涡虫的实验，赋予这个动词现代实验室含义。

items.en: The first date and the exact route from theology to biology are not fully recorded; dates here are approximate.
items.cn: 首见年代以及从神学到生物学的确切路径并无完整记录；此处年代为约数。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same generare family; group two holds near meanings that differ in agency and scope.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 generare 词族的形近词；第二组是近义词，区别在于施动者与范围。

entries.tag: the noun of the same act
entries.definition: The process or instance of regrowing. It names the event, while regenerate names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指再生这一过程或实例；regeneration 命名事件，regenerate 命名动作。

entries.definition: To bring something into being for the first time. It lacks the idea of a second life.
entries.definitionCN: 指首次产生某物；不含「第二次生命」的意思。

entries.definition: To fall from a better to a worse state, built with de- 'down'. It is the opposite of regenerate.
entries.definitionCN: 指由较好状态退向较差状态，由 de-「向下」构成，与 regenerate 相反。

entries.definition: Describing something able to renew itself, such as regenerative agriculture. It does not name the act.
entries.definitionCN: 形容能够自我更新的事物，如再生农业；它不命名动作本身。

entries.definition: To grow again after being cut. It is the everyday word for plants and hair, with no wider institutional sense.
entries.definitionCN: 指被剪后重新生长，是植物与头发的日常用词，没有更广的制度义。

entries.definition: To bring something back to a chosen earlier condition. It implies an agent doing the work, not self-renewal.
entries.definitionCN: 指通过有意的工作把某物带回选定的旧状态；暗含施动者，而非自行更新。

entries.definition: To make conscious or active again, from Latin vivere 'to live'. It suits practices and feelings more than tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 指出自拉丁 vivere「活」的使复苏，多用于习俗与感受，少用于组织。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + generare 'to beget': to give birth to again.
normal.cn: re-「再一次」+ generare「生育」：再生一次。

normal.en: The family runs generate, regenerate, regeneration, regenerative, degenerate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 generate、regenerate、regeneration、regenerative、degenerate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: regenerate tissue, regenerate forests, regenerate a neighbourhood.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：再生组织、使森林更新、复兴街区。

normal.en: Biology pairs it with tissue; forestry pairs it with stump and seed tree.
normal.cn: 生物学把它与组织配对；林学把它与树桩、母树配对。

normal.en: Engineering pairs it with resin and catalyst: a material given a second working life.
normal.cn: 工程学把它与树脂、催化剂配对：材料获得第二个使用周期。

abstract.en: Picture a willow rod pushed into wet soil and sprouting at its cut end.
abstract.cn: 想象一根柳条插进湿土，在切口处抽芽。

abstract.en: Picture a rusted dock rebuilt into a market square.
abstract.cn: 想象生锈的码头被改建成集市广场。

abstract.en: Picture a burnt forest floor already dotted with green shoots.
abstract.cn: 想象烧过的林地地面已点缀着绿芽。

examples.en: The liver can regenerate much of its tissue after surgery.
examples.cn: 肝脏在手术后能再生出大部分组织。

examples.en: Fire is part of the cycle that regenerates these grasslands.
examples.cn: 火是使这些草原更新的循环的一部分。

examples.en: The trust aims to regenerate the abandoned mill district.
examples.cn: 该基金会旨在复兴废弃的磨坊区。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞（re）生（generate）」——再来一次生成 → 再生、更新

root: 拉丁 re-「再一次」+ generare「生育」（源自 genus「出生、族类」）→ regenerare「再次产生」；英语 16 世纪进入，先用于神学，后用于生物学。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one action: what was lost, cut or worn down is made to grow or work again, from a lizard's tail to a forest, a district, a material and a purpose.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：失去、被截断或耗损的东西重新长出或重新运转，从蜥蜴尾巴到森林、街区、材料与目标感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cut stem that pushes a fresh shoot out of its wound.
core.cn: 核心意象：被截断的枝条从伤口处抽出新芽。

branches.en: LIVING REGROWTH: tissue and plants rebuild what was removed.
branches.cn: 活体再长：组织与植物重建被移除的部分。

branches.en: PLACE AND SYSTEM: districts and economies are given new activity.
branches.cn: 地点与系统：街区与经济获得新的活动。

branches.en: ECOSYSTEM: structure and function are restored, not just individuals.
branches.cn: 生态系统：恢复的是结构与功能，而非个体。

branches.en: MATERIAL: a spent medium returns to service.
branches.cn: 材料：用过的介质重新投入使用。

branches.en: SPIRIT AND RECORD: purpose is renewed, and objects are rebuilt from information.
branches.cn: 精神与记录：目标感被更新，物体依信息重建。

intro.en: The verb is Latin re- plus generare, with the usual English verb ending -ate; the noun and adjective shift to -ation and -ative.
intro.cn: 这个动词是拉丁 re- 加 generare，带常见英语动词词尾 -ate；名词与形容词分别转为 -ation 与 -ative。

latinIntro.en: Latin generare yields generate, regenerate, regeneration, regenerative, generation and generous.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 generare 衍生 generate、regenerate、regeneration、regenerative、generation 与 generous。

items.example: The moss regenerates after the dry season.
items.exampleCN: 苔藓在旱季之后再生。

items.example: Regeneration of the dune grass followed the storm.
items.exampleCN: 风暴之后沙丘草开始再生。

items.example: Regenerative grazing mimics wild herds.
items.exampleCN: 再生放牧模仿野生兽群。

items.meaning: a device or person that renews
items.example: The regenerator reheats the incoming air.
items.exampleCN: 回热器重新加热进入的空气。

items.example: The falls generate electricity.
items.exampleCN: 这道瀑布发电。

items.meaning: a producing; one stage of descent
items.example: A generation of seedlings grew under the gap.
items.exampleCN: 林隙下长起了一代幼苗。

items.meaning: to decline from a former kind
items.example: The cells degenerate without oxygen.
items.exampleCN: 没有氧，细胞会退化。

items.example: A generous rain ended the drought.
items.exampleCN: 一场充沛的雨结束了干旱。

definition_zh: 恢复生态学；研究如何修复与重建受损生态系统的学科
definition_en: the branch of ecology that studies how damaged ecosystems can be repaired and returned to a self-sustaining state
core_image: 矿坑复垦现场，工人把草皮一块块铺回坡面，木桩围出目标群落的样方
scene: 矿坑复垦现场，工人把草皮铺回坡面，木桩围出目标群落的样方。Restoration ecology asks how a mined slope can be returned to a self-sustaining grassland.
sceneCN: 这里 restoration ecology 指「恢复生态学」（第 1 个义项：研究受损生态系统如何修复并恢复自我维持能力的学科）；句意：恢复生态学追问一座矿坑坡地如何能被还原为自我维持的草地。图中可辨识物件：铺回的草皮、样方木桩、坡度标尺、目标群落草图。

pos.zh: 恢复生态学（不可数，作学科名）

senses.title: The discipline itself
senses.titleCN: 学科名：研究修复的生态学分支
senses.definition: the academic field that studies the repair of damaged ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 研究受损生态系统修复的学术领域
senses.example: Restoration ecology grew out of practical land reclamation after the 1980s.
senses.exampleCN: 恢复生态学在 20 世纪 80 年代之后从土地复垦实践中发展起来。
senses.why: restoration names putting something back and ecology names the study of households of nature, so the compound names the science of putting habitats back.
senses.whyCN: restoration 指放回原处，ecology 指研究自然家园的学问，因此这个复合词就是「把生境放回去」的科学。

senses.title: Its applied practice
senses.titleCN: 修复实践：把原理落到地块上
senses.definition: the practice of applying ecological principles to repair a specific site
senses.definitionCN: 把生态学原理应用到具体地块进行修复的实践
senses.example: Restoration ecology guided the replanting of the salt marsh.
senses.exampleCN: 恢复生态学指导了这片盐沼的重新种植。
senses.why: a discipline is also the work its practitioners do, so the same phrase names both the field and the fieldwork.
senses.whyCN: 学科也是从业者所做的工作，因此同一短语既指领域，也指野外作业。

senses.title: The reference ecosystem framework
senses.titleCN: 参照生态系统：拿什么当目标
senses.definition: the use of a healthy analogue site as the model for what a damaged site should become
senses.definitionCN: 以健康的同类地点作为受损地点应恢复成什么样的模板
senses.example: Restoration ecology relies on a nearby reference ecosystem for targets.
senses.exampleCN: 恢复生态学依赖附近一个参照生态系统来设定目标。
senses.why: without a model, 'restored' has no meaning, so the field builds its method around a reference site.
senses.whyCN: 没有模板，「已修复」就无从定义，因此这门学科围绕参照地建立方法。

senses.title: Assisted recovery of degraded land
senses.titleCN: 退化土地辅助恢复：帮它自己长回来
senses.definition: the theory of giving degraded land the conditions it needs to recover largely on its own
senses.definitionCN: 为退化土地提供条件、使其主要靠自身恢复的理论
senses.example: Restoration ecology prefers removing the cause over replanting every square metre.
senses.exampleCN: 恢复生态学更倾向于消除成因，而不是逐平方米补种。
senses.why: the field learned that ecosystems have their own repair capacity, so assistance is designed to release it.
senses.whyCN: 这门学科认识到生态系统自有修复能力，因此辅助措施是为了释放这种能力。

senses.title: Assembly and succession theory
senses.titleCN: 群落组建与演替理论
senses.definition: the theory of which species arrive in what order and how communities assemble
senses.definitionCN: 关于哪些物种以何种顺序到达、群落如何组建的理论
senses.example: Restoration ecology tests assembly rules by sowing species in different orders.
senses.exampleCN: 恢复生态学通过按不同顺序播种来检验组建规则。
senses.why: a restored site is a community being built, so the field borrows succession and assembly theory from ecology.
senses.whyCN: 修复地是一个正在建成的群落，因此这门学科借用生态学中的演替与组建理论。

senses.title: Monitoring and success criteria
senses.titleCN: 监测与成功标准：怎样算修好
senses.definition: the design of measurable criteria and long-term monitoring to judge whether restoration worked
senses.definitionCN: 设计可测量的标准与长期监测，以判断修复是否成功
senses.example: Restoration ecology defines success by function, not by the number of plants planted.
senses.exampleCN: 恢复生态学以功能而非栽种数量来定义成功。
senses.why: a project needs a stopping rule, so the discipline turns vague hopes into indicators that can be measured.
senses.whyCN: 项目需要停止规则，因此这门学科把模糊的期望变成可测量的指标。

senses.title: Its relation to conservation biology
senses.titleCN: 与保护生物学的关系
senses.definition: the subfield's position between protecting intact habitats and repairing damaged ones
senses.definitionCN: 该分支在保护完好生境与修复受损生境之间的位置
senses.example: Restoration ecology is often taught alongside conservation biology.
senses.exampleCN: 恢复生态学常与保护生物学一起教授。
senses.why: conservation guards what remains while restoration repairs what is gone, so the two fields share theory and differ in action.
senses.whyCN: 保护守住尚存之物，恢复修补已失之物，两者共享理论而行动不同。

senses.title: The social and community dimension
senses.titleCN: 社会与社区维度：谁来修、为谁修
senses.definition: the part of the field concerned with local participation, land tenure and social goals
senses.definitionCN: 关注本地参与、土地权属与社会目标的那部分内容
senses.example: Restoration ecology now includes community employment in its project design.
senses.exampleCN: 恢复生态学如今把社区就业纳入项目设计。
senses.why: restoration happens on someone's land and for someone's benefit, so the field had to take people into account.
senses.whyCN: 修复发生在别人的土地上、为别人的利益服务，因此这门学科必须把人纳入考量。

intro.en: Restoration ecology joins restoration, from Latin restaurare 'to renew', to ecology, coined from Greek oikos 'house' and -logia 'study'. The compound is recent, and dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: restoration ecology 把出自拉丁 restaurare「更新」的 restoration 与由希腊 oikos「家」和 -logia「学问」构成的 ecology 组合起来。这个复合词很新，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Restaurare meant 'to renew, restore'. Its second element is reconstructed as -staurare and is often linked to stare 'to stand', but the derivation is uncertain.
items.cn: restaurare 意为「更新、恢复」。其后一成分被重构为 -staurare，常与 stare「站立」联系，但这一推导并不确定。

items.en: Oikos meant 'house, dwelling, household', the base of economy as household management and of ecology as the study of nature's household.
items.cn: oikos 意为「房屋、住所、家户」，既是 economy「家政管理」的词根，也是 ecology「自然家户之学」的词根。

items.en: Ernst Haeckel coined Ökologie in 1866 for the study of the relations of organisms to their surroundings.
items.cn: 恩斯特·海克尔于 1866 年造出 Ökologie 一词，指研究生物与其环境关系的学问。

items.en: Ecology entered English in the 1870s; its adjective ecological followed within a decade.
items.cn: ecology 于 19 世纪 70 年代进入英语，其形容词 ecological 在十年内出现。

items.en: Restoration ecology became a named field in the 1980s, and the Society for Ecological Restoration was founded in 1988.
items.cn: 恢复生态学在 20 世纪 80 年代成为有名称的领域，国际生态修复学会于 1988 年成立。

items.en: The first use of the exact compound is not settled; earlier restoration projects exist without the name.
items.cn: 这一确切复合词的首用时间尚无定论；更早的修复工程已经存在，只是没有这个名称。

note.en: Group one holds the two words that make up the phrase; group two holds neighbouring fields and practices.
note.cn: 第一组是构成这个短语的两个词；第二组是相邻的学科与实践。

entries.definition: The act of putting something back into an earlier condition. It could refer to a painting or a building, not only to land.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物放回旧状态的行为，也可以指油画或建筑，不限于土地。

entries.definition: The study of organisms and their surroundings. On its own it says nothing about repair.
entries.definitionCN: 指研究生物与其环境的学问；单独使用时与修复无关。

entries.definition: The activity of repairing an ecosystem. Restoration ecology is the academic study of that activity.
entries.definitionCN: 指修复生态系统的活动；恢复生态学是对这一活动的学术研究。

entries.tag: a person or a political label
entries.definition: One who restores, often used of political movements aiming to bring back an old order.
entries.definitionCN: 指从事修复的人，也常用于主张恢复旧秩序的政治运动。

entries.definition: The science of protecting existing biodiversity. It guards intact habitat, while restoration ecology repairs damaged habitat.
entries.definitionCN: 指保护现存生物多样性的科学；它守住完好生境，恢复生态学修复受损生境。

entries.definition: Making damaged land useful again, often for a new purpose. It need not aim at the original community.
entries.definitionCN: 指使受损土地重新可用，常指向新用途；不必以原有群落为目标。

entries.definition: Converting derelict or mined land into usable ground, typically for agriculture or building.
entries.definitionCN: 指把废弃或采矿土地改造成可用地面，通常用于农业或建设。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: restoration 'putting back' + ecology 'study of the household': the science of putting habitats back.
normal.cn: restoration「放回」+ ecology「研究家户」：把生境放回去的学问。

normal.en: The family runs restore, restoration, ecological, ecology, ecologist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 restore、restoration、ecological、ecology、ecologist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: reference ecosystem, restoration site, principles of restoration ecology.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：参照生态系统、修复地、恢复生态学原理。

normal.en: The field pairs with conservation biology: one guards, the other repairs.
normal.cn: 这门学科与保护生物学配对：一个守护，一个修复。

normal.en: Its method starts from a reference site rather than from a blank plan.
normal.cn: 它的方法从参照地出发，而不是从空白方案出发。

abstract.en: Picture a doctor for landscapes: diagnose the damage, then help the patient heal.
abstract.cn: 想象一位景观医生：先诊断损伤，再帮病人自愈。

abstract.en: Picture a patch of bare mine spoil gradually closing over with grass.
abstract.cn: 想象一片裸露的矿渣地逐渐被草覆盖。

abstract.en: Picture an old photo used as the model for rebuilding a ruined square.
abstract.cn: 想象用一张旧照片作模板重建被毁的广场。

examples.en: Restoration ecology treats a healthy marsh nearby as the reference.
examples.cn: 恢复生态学把附近一片健康沼泽作为参照。

examples.en: Students of restoration ecology spend a full season monitoring planted plots.
examples.cn: 恢复生态学的学生要花整整一季监测栽种样地。

examples.en: Restoration ecology cannot promise a return to a pre-industrial landscape.
examples.cn: 恢复生态学无法保证回到工业化之前的景观。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「修复 + 生态学」——把坏掉的生境送进「生态修理铺」→ 研究如何修复受损生态系统的学科

root: 拉丁 restaurare「更新、恢复」（后一成分 -staurare 为重构形式，与 stare「站立」的联系不确定）+ 希腊 oikos「家户」与 -logia「学问」，由海克尔 1866 年造出 ecology；复合术语形成于 20 世纪 80 年代。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one project: a damaged site is compared with a reference, helped to heal, monitored and judged, all within a wider social setting.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个项目展开：受损地块与参照地比较、获得辅助而自愈、被监测与评估，并处在更广的社会情境中。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stripped slope where turf is laid back and stakes mark the target community.
core.cn: 核心意象：裸露的坡地铺回草皮，木桩标出目标群落。

branches.en: FIELD AND WORK: the same phrase names the discipline and its practice.
branches.cn: 学科与作业：同一短语既指学科，也指实践。

branches.en: MODEL AND NUDGE: a reference site sets the target, and assistance releases self-repair.
branches.cn: 模板与助推：参照地设定目标，辅助释放自愈能力。

branches.en: ASSEMBLY: succession and arrival order decide what community forms.
branches.cn: 组建：演替与到达顺序决定形成什么群落。

branches.en: VERDICT: success is measured by function, not by effort spent.
branches.cn: 判定：成功以功能衡量，而非以投入衡量。

branches.en: NEIGHBOURS AND PEOPLE: the field sits beside conservation and depends on landowners.
branches.cn: 邻域与人：这门学科与保护生物学相邻，并依赖土地所有者。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived noun in -ation to a Greek-derived noun in -logy; both halves are free words rather than root plus suffix.
intro.cn: 这个短语把带 -ation 的拉丁来源名词与带 -logy 的希腊来源名词并置；两半都是独立单词，而非词根加后缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin restaurare gives restore, restoration and restorative; Greek oikos with -logia gives ecology, ecological, ecologist and ecosystem.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 restaurare 衍生 restore、restoration 与 restorative；希腊 oikos 加 -logia 衍生 ecology、ecological、ecologist 与 ecosystem。

items.meaning: the study of putting habitats back
items.example: Restoration ecology is taught in forestry schools.
items.exampleCN: 林学院开设恢复生态学课程。

items.meaning: to put back into an earlier state
items.example: Crews restored the eroded bank with willow bundles.
items.exampleCN: 施工队用柳捆修复了被冲刷的河岸。

items.example: The restoration of the fen took twenty years.
items.exampleCN: 这片沼泽的修复用了二十年。

items.example: Fire can be restorative in a pine savanna.
items.exampleCN: 在松树稀树草原上，火可以有恢复作用。

items.meaning: the study of organisms and their surroundings
items.meaningCN: 研究生物与其环境的学问
items.example: Ecology treats a marsh as a system.
items.exampleCN: 生态学把沼泽当作一个系统。

items.example: The project set ecological targets first.
items.exampleCN: 该项目先设定生态目标。

items.example: An ecologist mapped the reference site.
items.exampleCN: 一位生态学家绘制了参照地。

items.meaning: a community plus its physical setting
items.meaningCN: 生物群落与其物理环境
items.example: The whole ecosystem was surveyed before planting.
items.exampleCN: 栽种之前对整个生态系统做了调查。

definition_zh: 进化论者；支持进化论的人；（作定语）进化论的
definition_en: a person who accepts or advocates the theory of biological evolution
core_image: 一位学者站在挂满地层与化石的墙前，用粉笔把一条从鱼到四足动物的箭头连起来
scene: 博物馆展厅里，一位学者沿着化石墙把鱼鳍到前肢的骨骼一一对应起来。The evolutionist traced each bone from fin to limb and argued that the two forms were related.
sceneCN: 这里 evolutionist 指「进化论者」（第 1 个义项：接受或主张生物进化论的人）；句意：这位进化论者把每块骨头从鳍到肢一一对应，论证两种形态具有亲缘关系。图中可辨识物件：化石墙、鱼鳍骨骼、前肢骨骼、粉笔箭头。

pos.zh: 进化论者；支持进化论的人（可数，复数为 evolutionists）
进化论的（作定语，如 evolutionist view）

senses.title: A supporter of biological evolution
senses.titleCN: 生物进化论的支持者
senses.definition: a person who accepts the theory that species change through descent with modification
senses.definitionCN: 接受物种经由共同祖先与变异而演变这一理论的人
senses.example: As a convinced evolutionist, she treated the fossil series as evidence of descent.
