senses.exampleCN: 作为坚定的进化论者，她把这一化石序列视为共同祖先的证据。
senses.why: -ist marks a person who holds a doctrine, so evolutionist names the holder of the evolution doctrine.
senses.whyCN: -ist 标记持某种学说的人，因此 evolutionist 指进化论这一学说的持有者。

senses.title: A scientist who studies evolution
senses.titleCN: 研究进化的学者
senses.definition: a researcher whose professional work is the study of evolutionary processes
senses.definitionCN: 以研究进化过程为专业工作的研究者
senses.example: The evolutionist compared fin bones across three lineages.
senses.exampleCN: 这位进化研究者比较了三个谱系的鳍骨。
senses.why: the label can shift from belief to profession, naming the person who works on the process rather than merely accepting it.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签可从信念转到职业，指实际研究该过程的人，而不只是接受该理论的人。

senses.title: A social evolutionist
senses.titleCN: 社会进化论者：把进化观用于社会
senses.definition: a person who applies evolutionary ideas to the development of societies
senses.definitionCN: 把进化观念用于社会发展的论者
senses.example: Nineteenth-century social evolutionists ranked societies on a single ladder.
senses.exampleCN: 19 世纪的社会进化论者把社会排在同一条阶梯上。
senses.why: the suffix travels to other fields, so the word can name someone applying selection and progress language to culture.
senses.whyCN: 这个后缀可迁移到其他领域，因此该词也指把选择与进步话语用于文化的人。

senses.title: Attributive use: evolutionist thinking
senses.titleCN: 定语用法：进化论的（观点、论证）
senses.definition: used before a noun to mean 'of or belonging to the evolutionist position'
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，表示「属于进化论立场的」
senses.example: The paper reviewed the evolutionist argument without endorsing it.
senses.exampleCN: 这篇论文评述了进化论论证，但并未为其背书。
senses.why: English lets an agent noun work as a modifier, so the person label becomes an adjective of stance.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许施动名词作修饰语，于是指人的标签变成表立场的定语。

senses.title: The opposing label in a debate
senses.titleCN: 论战中的对举标签：与神创论者相对
senses.definition: a term used for one side in public disputes over creation and evolution
senses.definitionCN: 在关于创造与进化的公共争论中指其中一方
senses.example: In the 1925 trial the evolutionist and the creationist were pitted against each other.
senses.exampleCN: 1925 年的那场审判里，进化论者与神创论者被摆在对立面。
senses.why: labels harden when a debate has two sides, so the word becomes a team name as much as a description.
senses.whyCN: 当争论分成两方，标签就会硬化，于是这个词既是描述，也是阵营名。

senses.title: One who applies evolutionary thinking elsewhere
senses.titleCN: 跨领域应用者：把进化思维用于别处
senses.definition: a person who extends evolutionary reasoning to language, technology or behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 把进化推理扩展到语言、技术或行为的人
senses.example: An evolutionist of language studies how words survive in use.
senses.exampleCN: 语言进化论者研究词语如何在使用中存活。
senses.why: once the mechanism is abstracted from biology, its advocates in other fields also carry the name.
senses.whyCN: 一旦机制从生物学中抽象出来，其他领域的倡导者也带上这个名称。

senses.title: A historical label for pre-Darwinian transformists
senses.titleCN: 历史标签：达尔文之前的转变论者
senses.definition: a term used for earlier thinkers who held that species change, before Darwin's mechanism
senses.definitionCN: 指在达尔文机制之前就主张物种会变化的早期思想家
senses.example: Lamarck is often called an evolutionist avant la lettre.
senses.exampleCN: 拉马克常被称为「尚未有该词之时的进化论者」。
senses.why: historians apply a later label backwards, so the word can name thinkers who lacked the mechanism but held the change.
senses.whyCN: 史学家把后来的标签回溯使用，因此该词可指没有机制、但主张变化的思想家。

senses.title: A loose or pejorative use
senses.titleCN: 泛称或贬义：被对手当作贬号
senses.definition: a loose label for anyone seen as pushing evolutionary ideas too far
senses.definitionCN: 对任何被认为过度推行进化观念者的泛称或贬称
senses.example: The critic dismissed the plan as the work of evolutionists.
senses.exampleCN: 批评者轻蔑地把该方案说成进化论者的产物。
senses.why: an -ist label can be used to dismiss, so the word sometimes says more about the speaker than the person named.
senses.whyCN: -ist 标签可用于贬斥，因此这个词有时更多反映说话者，而非被指者。

intro.en: Evolutionist joins evolution, from Latin evolutio 'an unrolling', to the agent suffix -ist. The word is a nineteenth-century formation, and dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: evolutionist 由出自拉丁 evolutio「展开」的 evolution 加施动后缀 -ist 构成，是 19 世纪的造词，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Volvere meant 'to roll, turn'; its compounds include revolvere 'to roll back' and involvere 'to wrap up'.
items.cn: volvere 意为「滚动、转动」，其复合词包括 revolvere「卷回」与 involvere「包卷」。

items.en: E- 'out' plus volvere gave evolvere 'to roll out, unroll', as when a scroll is opened.
items.cn: e-「向外」加 volvere 得 evolvere「展开、铺开」，如展开一卷书。

items.en: Evolutio named the act of unrolling; English evolution first meant the unfolding of a plan or a book.
items.cn: evolutio 指展开的动作；英语 evolution 最初指计划或书卷的展开。

items.en: By the early nineteenth century evolution was used for the gradual development of species, and Darwin fixed the modern sense in 1859.
items.cn: 到 19 世纪初，evolution 已用于指物种的逐步发展，达尔文于 1859 年确定了现代含义。

items.en: The agent noun evolutionist appears in the early nineteenth century for those who held that species change.
items.cn: 施动名词 evolutionist 出现于 19 世纪初，指主张物种会变化的人。

items.en: The exact first citation of evolutionist is uncertain, and its shift from belief to profession is not dated to a single text.
items.cn: evolutionist 的确切最早书证不确定；它从信念转为职业的转变也无法归到某一文本。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same volvere family; group two holds labels for people on either side of the debate.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 volvere 词族的形近词；第二组是争论双方的人物标签。

entries.definition: The unfolding or change of a lineage. Evolutionist names a person who accepts or studies it.
entries.definitionCN: 指谱系的展开或变化；evolutionist 指接受或研究它的人。

entries.definition: Relating to evolution, as in evolutionary biology. It describes ideas or processes, not a holder of them.
entries.definitionCN: 指与进化相关的，如进化生物学；描述观念或过程，而非持有者。

entries.definition: The system of belief that evolution explains change, sometimes extended to society. Evolutionist is the person who holds it.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为进化能解释变化的信念体系，有时扩展到社会；evolutionist 是持有该体系的人。

entries.definition: To develop gradually. It can be used of species, plans or opinions, without any person label.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐步发展，可用于物种、计划或观点，不含人物标签。

entries.definition: One who accepts Darwin's specific mechanism of natural selection. All Darwinists are evolutionists, but not all evolutionists are Darwinists.
entries.definitionCN: 指接受达尔文具体自然选择机制的人；达尔文主义者都是进化论者，反之不然。

entries.definition: One who holds that life was created directly rather than descended. It is the usual counterpart in public debate.
entries.definitionCN: 指认为生命被直接创造而非演化而来的人，是公共争论中常见的对立标签。

entries.definition: An older word for one who holds that species transform over time, used before evolution became standard.
entries.definitionCN: 指主张物种随时间转变的较早用词，在 evolution 成为标准说法之前使用。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: evolution 'unrolling' + -ist 'one who holds': one who holds the unrolling view of life.
normal.cn: evolution「展开」+ -ist「持有者」：持有生命展开观的人。

normal.en: The family runs evolve, evolution, evolutionary, evolutionism, evolutionist.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 evolve、evolution、evolutionary、evolutionism、evolutionist。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: convinced evolutionist, social evolutionist, evolutionist argument.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：坚定的进化论者、社会进化论者、进化论论证。

normal.en: Pair it with Darwinist: the wider label versus the narrower one.
normal.cn: 把它与 Darwinist 配对：一个更宽，一个更窄。

normal.en: Pair it with creationist: the two sides of the same public argument.
normal.cn: 把它与 creationist 配对：同一场公共争论的两方。

abstract.en: Picture a scholar joining fin bones to limb bones with chalk lines.
abstract.cn: 想象一位学者用粉笔把鳍骨与肢骨连成线。

abstract.en: Picture a family tree drawn over a wall of fossils.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅画在化石墙上的家族树。

abstract.en: Picture two debaters on a stage, each with a fixed label.
abstract.cn: 想象台上两位辩手，各自带着固定标签。

examples.en: The evolutionist argued that the shared bones implied shared ancestry.
examples.cn: 这位进化论者论证共有骨骼意味着共同祖先。

examples.en: Social evolutionists of the nineteenth century often ranked cultures in a single line.
examples.cn: 19 世纪的社会进化论者常把各种文化排成一条单线。

examples.en: The court case turned evolutionists and creationists into public camps.
examples.cn: 那场官司把进化论者与神创论者变成了公开的阵营。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「进化（evolution）+ 人（-ist）」——相信生命是一卷慢慢展开的画轴的人 → 进化论者

root: 拉丁 e-「向外」+ volvere「滚动」→ evolvere「展开」→ evolutio「展开」；英语 evolution 先指书卷或计划的展开，19 世纪转指物种演变，加 -ist 构成 evolutionist。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a believer to a researcher, then to social and attributive uses, a debate camp, a cross-field label, a historical label and finally a dismissal.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从信众到研究者，再到社会用法与定语用法、争论阵营、跨领域标签、历史标签，最后落到贬称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scholar drawing a line from a fin bone to a limb bone.
core.cn: 核心意象：一位学者把鳍骨与肢骨连成一线。

branches.en: BELIEF AND WORK: the same label covers those who accept the theory and those who study it.
branches.cn: 信念与工作：同一标签既指接受理论者，也指研究理论者。

branches.en: EXTENSION: the label travels to society, language and technology.
branches.cn: 外延：标签迁移到社会、语言与技术。

branches.en: MODIFIER: the person word becomes a stance adjective.
branches.cn: 修饰语：指人名词转为表立场的定语。

branches.en: CAMPS: in debate the label hardens into a team name or an insult.
branches.cn: 阵营：在争论中标签硬化为队名或贬称。

branches.en: HINDSIGHT: historians apply the later label to earlier thinkers.
branches.cn: 回溯：史学家把后来的标签用于更早的思想家。

intro.en: The noun is evolution plus the agent suffix -ist; evolution itself is a Latin-derived noun in -ion from evolvere.
intro.cn: 这个名词是 evolution 加施动后缀 -ist；evolution 本身是由 evolvere 派生的带 -ion 拉丁来源名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin volvere and evolvere yield evolve, evolution, evolutionary, evolutionism, evolutionist and involve, revolve, volume.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 volvere 与 evolvere 衍生 evolve、evolution、evolutionary、evolutionism、evolutionist，以及 involve、revolve、volume。

items.meaning: one who holds or studies evolution
items.meaningCN: 持有或研究进化论的人
items.example: The evolutionist compared three fossil series.
items.exampleCN: 这位进化论者比较了三个化石序列。

items.example: The evolution of the eye is a classic case.
items.exampleCN: 眼睛的进化是经典案例。

items.example: An evolutionary tree links the lineages.
items.exampleCN: 一棵进化树把各谱系连起来。

items.meaning: the doctrine that evolution explains change
items.meaningCN: 认为进化能解释变化的学说
items.example: Social evolutionism shaped Victorian anthropology.
items.exampleCN: 社会进化主义塑造了维多利亚时代的人类学。

items.example: The book took an evolutionistic line.
items.exampleCN: 这本书采取进化论的立场。

items.example: The fin evolved into a limb.
items.exampleCN: 鳍逐渐进化成肢。

items.example: The survey involved three field seasons.
items.exampleCN: 这项调查涉及三个野外季节。

items.meaning: to roll back; to go round
items.example: The debate revolved around one fossil.
items.exampleCN: 争论围绕一块化石打转。

definition_zh: 自然选择；达尔文提出的机制：可遗传变异中较适应者留下更多后代
definition_en: the process by which individuals with heritable traits that suit their environment leave more offspring, so those traits spread
core_image: 一片雪地上并排站着深色与浅色两种小兽，浅色的几乎看不见，深色的被上方影子标出，旁边画着「下一代」的箭头
scene: 雪地里两群颜色不同的小兽被同一只猛禽搜寻，浅色的几乎融进背景，深色的先被看见。Over many winters, natural selection favoured the lighter coat and the darker ones became rare.
sceneCN: 这里 natural selection 指「自然选择」（第 1 个义项：达尔文提出的、由环境差异淘汰与保留可遗传变异的机制）；句意：经过许多个冬天，自然选择偏爱浅色皮毛，深色个体变得稀少。图中可辨识物件：雪地、深色与浅色小兽、猛禽影子、下一代箭头。

pos.zh: 自然选择（不可数，作生物学术语）

senses.title: Darwin's mechanism
senses.titleCN: 达尔文机制：差异生存与繁殖
senses.definition: the mechanism by which heritable variation that improves survival and reproduction becomes more common
senses.definitionCN: 使有利于生存与繁殖的可遗传变异变得更普遍的机制
senses.example: Darwin proposed natural selection as the main engine of descent with modification.
senses.exampleCN: 达尔文提出自然选择是伴有变异的共同祖先演变的主要动力。
senses.why: nature does the sorting: variants that leave more offspring are kept simply because they leave more copies.
senses.whyCN: 是大自然在做筛选：留下更多后代的变异被保留，只因它们留下了更多副本。

senses.title: Differential survival and reproduction
senses.titleCN: 差异生存与繁殖：留下不同数量的后代
senses.definition: the measurable difference in survival and reproductive output among variants
senses.definitionCN: 不同变异体在存活与繁殖产出上的可测量差异
senses.example: Natural selection requires that the variants differ in reproductive success.
senses.exampleCN: 自然选择要求各变异体在繁殖成功率上存在差异。
senses.why: the mechanism is not a force but a statistical outcome: some variants contribute more offspring than others.
senses.whyCN: 这一机制不是一种力，而是一个统计结果：某些变异体贡献的后代更多。

senses.title: Selection without a selector
senses.titleCN: 没有选择者的「选择」：一个隐喻
senses.definition: the metaphorical use of 'selection' for an outcome that involves no conscious chooser
senses.definitionCN: 用「选择」一词隐喻一个并无自觉选择者的结果
senses.example: The word selection in natural selection is a metaphor, not a claim about intent.
senses.exampleCN: 自然选择中的「选择」是隐喻，并不主张存在意图。
senses.why: the term borrows the breeder's language, which is why readers keep asking who does the choosing.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语借用了育种者的话，因此读者总在追问：到底谁在做选择。

senses.title: Contrast with artificial selection
senses.titleCN: 与人工选择对举
senses.definition: the natural counterpart of the breeder's deliberate choice of parents
senses.definitionCN: 与育种者有意挑选亲本相对的自然过程
senses.example: Darwin began with artificial selection in pigeons and then extended the logic to nature.
senses.exampleCN: 达尔文从鸽子的人工选择入手，再把这一逻辑推到自然界。
senses.why: the contrast explains the word: people select parents on purpose, while nature 'selects' by leaving different numbers of descendants.
senses.whyCN: 这一对照解释了词义：人有意挑选亲本，而自然通过留下不同数量的后代来「选择」。

senses.title: The unit or target of selection
senses.titleCN: 选择单位：个体、基因还是群体
senses.definition: the level at which selection is said to act, such as the individual, the gene or the group
senses.definitionCN: 选择被认为作用的层级，如个体、基因或群体
senses.example: Debate over the unit of natural selection shaped mid-twentieth-century biology.
senses.exampleCN: 关于自然选择单位的争论塑造了 20 世纪中期的生物学。
senses.why: once the mechanism is accepted, the next question is what exactly is being sorted, and the term is reused at each level.
senses.whyCN: 机制被接受之后，下一个问题是什么在被筛选，而术语在每个层级上都被重复使用。

senses.title: Directional or stabilising outcome
senses.titleCN: 选择方向：定向、稳定或分裂
senses.definition: the pattern selection produces, such as a shift, a narrowing or a split in a trait
senses.definitionCN: 选择产生的模式，如性状的移动、收窄或分裂
senses.example: Natural selection can be directional, stabilising or disruptive.
senses.exampleCN: 自然选择可以是定向的、稳定的或分裂的。
senses.why: the same mechanism yields different shapes depending on which variants survive, so the term covers all three outcomes.
senses.whyCN: 同一机制因存活变异不同而产生不同形状，因此这个术语涵盖三种结果。

senses.title: The modern synthesis formulation
senses.titleCN: 现代综合论表述：与遗传学合并
senses.definition: the twentieth-century version that combines selection with Mendelian genetics and population thinking
senses.definitionCN: 20 世纪把选择与孟德尔遗传学、群体思维结合的版本
senses.example: The modern synthesis restated natural selection in terms of allele frequencies.
senses.exampleCN: 现代综合论用等位基因频率重述了自然选择。
senses.why: genetics supplied the missing heredity, so the term gained a precise population-level definition.
senses.whyCN: 遗传学补上了缺失的遗传机制，于是这个术语获得了精确的群体层面定义。

senses.title: Popular shorthand for 'survival of the fittest'
senses.titleCN: 通俗简称：适者生存
senses.definition: the loose everyday use of the phrase for competition in general
senses.definitionCN: 日常中泛指竞争、常与「适者生存」混用的说法
senses.example: Popular writing often reduces natural selection to a single slogan.
senses.exampleCN: 通俗写作常把自然选择简化成一句口号。
senses.why: a phrase that names a precise mechanism gets flattened when it travels, and the flat version is worth recognising.
senses.whyCN: 一个指精确机制的短语在传播中会被压平，而这个压平的版本也值得识别。

intro.en: Natural selection joins natural, from Latin naturalis and natura 'nature', to selection, from Latin selectio 'a choosing out'. Darwin fixed the biological sense in 1859, and dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: natural selection 把出自拉丁 naturalis、natura「自然」的 natural 与出自拉丁 selectio「挑出」的 selection 组合起来；达尔文于 1859 年确定其生物学含义，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Natura 'nature' comes from nasci 'to be born'; naturalis meant 'of birth, of the ordinary course of things'.
items.cn: natura「自然」出自 nasci「出生」；naturalis 意为「与生俱来、属于事物常规进程的」。

items.en: Lego meant 'to gather, pick out'; its participle lectus underlies select, collect and elect.
items.cn: lego 意为「收集、挑出」；其分词 lectus 是 select、collect 与 elect 的基础。

items.en: Se- 'apart' plus legere gave seligere 'to pick out', and selectio named the picking out.
items.cn: se-「分开」加 legere 得 seligere「挑出」，selectio 指挑出的行为。

items.en: Natural entered English in the fourteenth century and selection in the seventeenth, both through French.
items.cn: natural 于 14 世纪进入英语，selection 于 17 世纪经法语进入。

items.en: Darwin used natural selection in On the Origin of Species to name the preservation of favourable variations.
items.cn: 达尔文在《物种起源》中用 natural selection 指有利变异的保存。

items.en: The 1930s and 1940s merged selection with genetics, and the term was restated in population terms; the exact wording varies by author.
items.cn: 20 世纪 30 至 40 年代把选择与遗传学合并，术语以群体语言重述；具体措辞因作者而异。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same legere family; group two holds mechanisms and slogans often confused with natural selection.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 legere 词族的形近词；第二组是常与自然选择混淆的机制与口号。

entries.definition: The act of picking out, used for books, teams and data as well as for organisms.
entries.definitionCN: 指挑出的行为，可用于书籍、队伍与数据，也可用于生物。

entries.definition: Tending to choose some and reject others, as in selective pressure or selective breeding.
entries.definitionCN: 指倾向于选择一部分而排斥另一部分，如选择压力或选择性育种。

entries.definition: The environmental force that makes some variants leave more offspring. Natural selection is the result of that pressure over generations.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某些变异留下更多后代的环境作用力；自然选择是这种压力在多代中产生的结果。

entries.definition: Breeders choosing parents on purpose. It shares the mechanism but replaces nature with human intent.
entries.definitionCN: 指育种者有意挑选亲本；机制相同，但以人的意图取代自然。

entries.definition: A phrase coined by Herbert Spencer and adopted by Darwin as shorthand; it invites the false reading that only strength matters.
entries.definitionCN: 由斯宾塞造出、被达尔文用作简称的短语；容易引出「只有强壮才重要」的误读。

entries.definition: A trait that improves survival or reproduction. Natural selection is the process that builds adaptations.
entries.definitionCN: 指提高生存或繁殖的性状；自然选择是塑造这些性状的过程。

entries.definition: Any change in the heritable traits of a population. Natural selection is one cause of evolution, not its synonym.
entries.definitionCN: 指群体可遗传性状的任何变化；自然选择是进化的一个原因，而非同义词。

entries.definition: Random change in allele frequencies, strongest in small populations. It produces evolution without natural selection.
entries.definitionCN: 指等位基因频率的随机变化，在小群体中最强；它能造成没有自然选择的进化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: natural 'of the ordinary course' + selection 'picking out': nature does the picking.
normal.cn: natural「属常规进程」+ selection「挑出」：由大自然来挑。

normal.en: The family runs select, selection, selective, natural, naturally.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 select、selection、selective、natural、naturally。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: by natural selection, theory of natural selection, natural selection pressure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：通过自然选择、自然选择理论、自然选择压力。

normal.en: Contrast it with artificial selection: the same sorting, a different chooser.
normal.cn: 把它与人工选择对照：同样的筛选，不同的选择者。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with evolution: selection is one cause, evolution is the change.
normal.cn: 不要与 evolution 混淆：选择是原因之一，进化是变化本身。

abstract.en: Picture two coats of fur on one snowy slope, one blending in and one standing out.
abstract.cn: 想象雪坡上两种毛色，一种融进背景，一种格外醒目。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve that keeps only grains above a certain size.
abstract.cn: 想象一只筛子，只留下超过某一大小的谷粒。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger where each variant's offspring are counted, year after year.
abstract.cn: 想象一本账，年复一年记录每种变异留下的后代。

examples.en: Natural selection can change a population without any deliberate breeding.
examples.cn: 自然选择无需任何有意的育种就能改变一个群体。

examples.en: The finches' beaks are a classic example of natural selection.
examples.cn: 雀鸟的喙是自然选择的经典例子。

examples.en: Antibiotic resistance in bacteria is natural selection in action.
examples.cn: 细菌的抗生素耐药性就是正在起作用的自然选择。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「自然在挑人」——不是谁在选，而是环境把留下的后代筛了一遍 → 自然选择

root: 拉丁 natura「自然」（出自 nasci「出生」）+ 拉丁 seligere「挑出」（se-「分开」+ legere「收集」）→ selectio「挑出」；达尔文 1859 年固定为生物学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from Darwin's mechanism to its measurable core, its metaphor, its contrast with breeding, its units, its directions, its genetic restatement and its popular flattening.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从达尔文机制走到可测量的核心、隐喻、与育种的对照、作用单位、方向、遗传学重述，最后落到通俗化的压平版本。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a snow slope where one coat blends in and another stands out, winter after winter.
core.cn: 核心意象：一片雪坡上，一种毛色融进背景，另一种格外醒目，年复一年。

branches.en: MECHANISM: heritable difference plus unequal reproduction equals a spread of traits.
branches.cn: 机制：可遗传差异加不均等繁殖，等于性状扩散。

branches.en: METAPHOR AND CONTRAST: 'selection' without a selector, set beside the breeder's choice.
branches.cn: 隐喻与对照：没有选择者的「选择」，与育种者的挑选并置。

branches.en: LEVELS AND DIRECTIONS: what is sorted, and which shape the sorting takes.
branches.cn: 层级与方向：被筛选的是什么，筛选又呈何种形状。

branches.en: GENETIC RESTATEMENT: allele frequencies give the mechanism a precise language.
branches.cn: 遗传学重述：等位基因频率为机制提供了精确语言。

branches.en: SLOGAN: the phrase is flattened into 'survival of the fittest'.
branches.cn: 口号：短语被压平成「适者生存」。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived adjective to a Latin-derived noun in -ion; selection is the noun of action from seligere.
intro.cn: 这个短语把拉丁来源形容词与带 -ion 的拉丁来源名词并置；selection 是 seligere 的表动作名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin legere and seligere yield select, selection, selective, collect, elect and intellect; Latin nasci yields nature, natural and native.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 legere 与 seligere 衍生 select、selection、selective、collect、elect 与 intellect；拉丁 nasci 衍生 nature、natural 与 native。

items.meaning: the picking out done by the ordinary course of nature
items.meaningCN: 由自然常规进程完成的挑选
items.example: Natural selection explains the match between beak and seed.
items.exampleCN: 自然选择解释了喙与种子的匹配。

items.example: Females select mates by song.
items.exampleCN: 雌性依据鸣声选择配偶。

items.example: Selection acts on the whole phenotype.
items.exampleCN: 选择作用于整个表型。

items.example: Selective logging leaves the smallest trees.
items.exampleCN: 选择性采伐留下最小的树。

items.meaning: one who or that which chooses
items.example: Nature is not a selector in the literal sense.
items.exampleCN: 自然并不是字面意义上的选择者。

items.example: The cliff is a natural shelter.
items.exampleCN: 这处崖壁是天然庇护所。

items.example: The population naturally fluctuates.
items.exampleCN: 该群体天然地波动。

items.example: The team collected seeds from the reference site.
items.exampleCN: 团队从参照地采集种子。

definition_zh: 选择压力；环境对群体中不同变异体生存与繁殖的差别性作用强度
definition_en: the strength of the environmental force that makes some variants survive and reproduce better than others
core_image: 一只手从上方压下，桌上一排高低不同的小柱，高柱被压弯、矮柱纹丝不动，旁边记着刻度与计数
scene: 实验室里，同一批细菌被分成两组，一组加抗生素、一组不加，加药的那组只有少数菌落存活。The antibiotic put strong selection pressure on the culture, and only resistant cells remained.
sceneCN: 这里 selection pressure 指「选择压力」（第 1 个义项：使不同变异体在生存上产生差别的作用强度）；句意：抗生素对这一培养物施加了很强的选择压力，最后只剩下耐药细胞。图中可辨识物件：培养皿、抗生素纸片、存活菌落、计数表格。

pos.zh: 选择压力（可数或不可数，复数为 selection pressures）

collocations.zh: 来自捕食者的选择压力

senses.title: The force behind differential survival
senses.titleCN: 差别生存的驱动力
senses.definition: the force that causes variants in a population to survive and reproduce at different rates
senses.definitionCN: 使群体内各变异体以不同速率存活与繁殖的作用力
senses.example: Predation placed heavy selection pressure on the slower moths.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食对行动较慢的蛾施加了沉重的选择压力。
senses.why: pressure names a push that is applied, so the phrase pictures the environment pressing on a population and sorting it.
senses.whyCN: pressure 指施加的推力，因此这个短语把环境想象成压在群体上并把它分选开来。

senses.title: Its measurable intensity
senses.titleCN: 强度：压力有多大
senses.definition: the quantified strength of selection, often expressed as a selection coefficient
senses.definitionCN: 选择的量化强度，常以选择系数表示
senses.example: The study estimated the selection pressure on beak depth.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究估算了喙深所受的选择压力强度。
senses.why: once the force is measured, it becomes a variable that can be compared across traits and populations.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这种力被测量，它就变成一个可跨性状、跨群体比较的变量。

senses.title: The source of the pressure
senses.titleCN: 压力来源：谁在施压
senses.definition: the specific agent, such as a predator, a disease or a climate, that applies the pressure
senses.definitionCN: 施加压力的具体因素，如捕食者、疾病或气候
senses.example: Drought is the main selection pressure in this grassland.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱是这片草地上的主要选择压力。
senses.why: the phrase can name either the force or its source, and ecology usually cares about which agent is doing the pushing.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语既可指力，也可指力的来源，而生态学通常关心是哪个因素在推。

senses.title: A directional bias on one trait
senses.titleCN: 方向性偏压：把某一性状往一边推
senses.definition: pressure that consistently favours one end of a trait's range over the other
senses.definitionCN: 持续偏向某一性状取值区间一端、而非另一端的压力
senses.example: Longer bills faced positive selection pressure during the dry years.
senses.exampleCN: 在干旱年份，较长的喙承受正向选择压力。
senses.why: when the same end keeps winning, the pressure acquires a direction, which is how new traits begin to shift.
senses.whyCN: 当同一端持续胜出，压力就有了方向，新性状正是这样开始移动的。

senses.title: A constraint that removes variants
senses.titleCN: 淘汰作用：把不适合的变异去掉
senses.definition: the part of the pressure that eliminates variants rather than promoting them
senses.definitionCN: 压力中负责淘汰而非促进变异的那一部分
senses.example: Frost imposes a selection pressure that weeds out early flowers.
senses.exampleCN: 霜冻施加选择压力，把早开花的个体淘汰掉。
senses.why: selection is often easier to see as removal: what disappears leaves a visible gap in the distribution.
senses.whyCN: 选择往往更容易被看成「移除」：消失的部分在分布上留下可见的空缺。

senses.title: Human-induced pressure
senses.titleCN: 人为压力：抗生素、捕捞与污染
senses.definition: selection pressure created by human activity, such as drugs, harvesting or pollution
senses.definitionCN: 由人类活动造成的选择压力，如药物、采捕或污染
senses.example: Trawling applies selection pressure for smaller adult fish.
senses.exampleCN: 拖网对体型更小的成鱼施加选择压力。
senses.why: people became the strongest source of pressure in many systems, so the phrase now carries a conservation warning.
senses.whyCN: 在许多系统里人已成为最强的压力来源，因此这个短语如今带有保护警示。

senses.title: Analogy outside biology
senses.titleCN: 生物学之外的类比用法
senses.definition: the extended use of the phrase for any environment that favours some variants over others
senses.definitionCN: 把这个短语扩展用于任何偏爱某些变体的环境
senses.example: The market put selection pressure on firms with thin cash reserves.
senses.exampleCN: 市场对现金储备薄弱的公司施加选择压力。
senses.why: once 'variant plus environment' is abstracted, the phrase fits markets, software and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 当「变体加环境」被抽象出来，这个短语就适用于市场、软件与机构。

senses.title: Relaxed or released pressure
senses.titleCN: 压力松弛：筛选变弱之后
senses.definition: the state in which selection pressure is reduced, allowing traits to drift or decline
senses.definitionCN: 选择压力减弱、使性状得以漂变或退化的状态
senses.example: With predators gone, selection pressure on armour relaxed.
senses.exampleCN: 捕食者消失后，对甲壳的选择压力松弛了。
senses.why: pressure is only visible when it is removed: traits that cost something then persist without being pruned.
senses.whyCN: 压力只在被移除时才显形：此后那些有代价的性状不再被修剪，得以留存。

intro.en: Selection pressure joins selectio 'a choosing out' to pressure, from Latin pressura 'a pressing', built on premere 'to press'. The ecological phrase is twentieth-century, and dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: selection pressure 把 selectio「挑出」与出自拉丁 pressura「压挤」、基于 premere「压」的 pressure 组合起来；这一生态短语形成于 20 世纪，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Legere 'to gather, pick out' underlies select, selection and selective through the compound seligere.
items.cn: legere「收集、挑出」经复合词 seligere 构成 select、selection 与 selective 的基础。

items.en: Premere meant 'to press, squeeze'; pressura named the act or result of pressing.
items.cn: premere 意为「压、挤」；pressura 指压的动作或结果。

items.en: Pressure entered English in the fourteenth century as a physical term and later acquired figurative senses.
items.cn: pressure 于 14 世纪作为物理术语进入英语，后来获得比喻义。

items.en: Nineteenth-century naturalists spoke of selection acting on variations, but the fixed phrase selection pressure is later.
items.cn: 19 世纪博物学者谈论选择作用于变异，但固定短语 selection pressure 出现得更晚。

items.en: Population genetics in the twentieth century made the phrase quantitative, tied to fitness differences and selection coefficients.
items.cn: 20 世纪的群体遗传学使这个短语定量化，与适合度差异和选择系数挂钩。

items.en: The exact first use of the compound is uncertain; earlier writers said 'pressure of selection' or 'selective pressure'.
items.cn: 这一复合词的确切首用不确定；更早的作者写作「选择的压力」或「选择性压力」。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same roots; group two holds related terms that name a different part of the evolutionary account.
note.cn: 第一组是同源形近词；第二组是相关术语，各自命名进化解释中的不同部分。

entries.definition: The same idea with an adjective instead of a noun, widely used in textbooks; the two are usually interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 同一概念改用形容词表达，教科书常用；二者通常可互换。

entries.definition: The outcome of differential survival. Pressure is the force that produces that outcome.
entries.definitionCN: 指差别生存的结果；压力是产生这一结果的作用力。

entries.definition: A force applied to something. On its own it need not be biological at all.
entries.definitionCN: 指施加于某物的力；单独使用时完全不必与生物有关。

entries.definition: Deliberate choice of parents by breeders. It produces artificial, not natural, selection pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指育种者有意挑选亲本，产生的是人工而非自然的选择压力。

entries.definition: The mechanism as a whole. Selection pressure is one way of measuring how hard that mechanism is pushing.
entries.definitionCN: 指整个机制；选择压力是衡量这一机制推力大小的一种方式。

entries.definition: The relative reproductive success of a variant. Pressure explains why fitness differs.
entries.definitionCN: 指变体的相对繁殖成功率；压力解释为何适合度会有差异。

entries.definition: A factor that limits what evolution can build, such as body plan or available variation; it is not the same as a pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指限制进化能造出什么的因素，如体型方案或可用变异；与压力不同。

entries.definition: An environmental condition that strains organisms. It may create selection pressure, but it is not the pressure itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指使生物承受压力的环境条件；它可能造成选择压力，但本身不是压力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: selection 'picking out' + pressure 'pressing': the environment pressing on a population and picking.
normal.cn: selection「挑选」+ pressure「压」：环境压向群体并挑选。

normal.en: The family runs select, selection, selective, pressure, press.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 select、selection、selective、pressure、press。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: strong pressure, pressure on a trait, under pressure, relieve pressure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：强压力、对某性状的压力、处于压力之下、缓解压力。

normal.en: Pair it with fitness: pressure explains why fitness scores differ.
normal.cn: 把它与 fitness 配对：压力解释为何适合度分数不同。

normal.en: Pair it with constraint: pressure pushes, constraint limits.
normal.cn: 把它与 constraint 配对：压力推动，约束限制。

abstract.en: Picture a hand flattening tall posts but leaving short ones upright.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手把高柱压弯，矮柱却直立不动。

abstract.en: Picture a sieve that lets small seeds through and holds large ones.
abstract.cn: 想象一只筛子让小的种子漏下，把大的留下。

abstract.en: Picture a trawl net that keeps only fish below a certain size.
abstract.cn: 想象一张拖网只留下小于某个尺寸的鱼。

examples.en: Selection pressure from predators favours faster runners.
examples.cn: 来自捕食者的选择压力偏爱跑得更快的个体。

examples.en: Removing the drug relieves selection pressure on resistant bacteria.
examples.cn: 停用药物会缓解耐药细菌所受的选择压力。

examples.en: The team measured selection pressure as a difference in survival rates.
examples.cn: 团队以存活率的差异来衡量选择压力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「挑选 + 压力」——环境像一只手掌，把不合格的压下去 → 选择压力

root: 拉丁 seligere「挑出」（se- + legere）+ 拉丁 premere「压」→ pressura「压挤」；生态与群体遗传学术语于 20 世纪定量化。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one push: a force is applied, measured, sourced, directed, seen as removal, traced to people, extended as an analogy and finally released.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一次推压展开：力被施加、被测量、被溯源、被定向、被看成淘汰、被人为放大、被当作类比，最后被松开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pressing down on a row of uneven posts, bending only some.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手压向一排高低不齐的柱子，只把其中一些压弯。

branches.en: FORCE AND MEASURE: the push exists, and then it is given a number.
branches.cn: 力与量：推力存在，随后被赋予数值。

branches.en: SOURCE AND DIRECTION: which agent pushes, and toward which end of the range.
branches.cn: 来源与方向：哪个因素在推，又推向取值区间的哪一端。

branches.en: REMOVAL AND RELEASE: pressure is clearest in what it deletes, and in what returns once it stops.
branches.cn: 淘汰与松弛：压力在它删去什么、以及停下后什么回流时最清楚。

branches.en: HUMAN SOURCE: drugs, nets and pollution become the strongest pressures.
branches.cn: 人为来源：药物、渔网与污染成为最强的压力。

branches.en: ANALOGY: markets and software inherit the same shape.
branches.cn: 类比：市场与软件继承了同一形状。

intro.en: The compound is two Latin-derived nouns; selection carries -ion and pressure carries -ure, both noun endings of action or result.
intro.cn: 这个复合词由两个拉丁来源名词构成：selection 带 -ion，pressure 带 -ure，两者都是表动作或结果的名词词尾。

latinIntro.en: Latin seligere gives select, selection and selective; Latin premere gives press, pressure, compress, express and suppress.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 seligere 衍生 select、selection 与 selective；拉丁 premere 衍生 press、pressure、compress、express 与 suppress。

items.example: Selection pressure shaped the beak within a decade.
items.exampleCN: 选择压力在十年内塑造了鸟喙。

items.example: Selection removed the weakest seedlings.
items.exampleCN: 筛选淘汰了最弱的幼苗。

items.example: The females select the loudest singers.
items.exampleCN: 雌性挑选叫声最响的个体。

items.example: Grazing is selective on tall grasses.
items.exampleCN: 放牧对高草具有选择性。

items.example: The pressure on the population never eased.
items.exampleCN: 这个群体所受的压力从未减轻。

items.example: The crowding pressed the plants into narrow forms.
items.exampleCN: 拥挤把植株压成窄小的形态。

items.example: The sediment compressed into shale.
items.exampleCN: 沉积物被压成页岩。

items.meaning: to press down; to hold back
items.example: Fire suppression removed a natural pressure.
items.exampleCN: 灭火措施移除了一种自然压力。

definition_zh: 适应压力；迫使生物、系统或组织调整自身以应对环境变化的作用力
definition_en: the force or demand that pushes an organism, system or organisation to adjust in order to cope with changed conditions
core_image: 一只鸟站在两种喙形轮廓之间，背景从左边的软果变成右边的硬壳，一条箭头由软果指向硬壳
scene: 岛上原本只有软果，后来漂来一批硬壳种子，鸟群只能啄开外壳才能进食。The new seed coat placed adaptation pressure on the birds and favoured deeper beaks.
sceneCN: 这里 adaptation pressure 指「适应压力」（第 1 个义项：迫使生物调整自身以应对新环境的作用）；句意：新的种皮对鸟群形成适应压力，偏爱更深的喙。图中可辨识物件：软果、硬壳种子、深浅不同的喙、选择箭头。

pos.zh: 适应压力（可数或不可数，复数为 adaptation pressures）

collocations.zh: 生境改变带来的适应压力

senses.title: The force that drives adaptive change
senses.titleCN: 驱动适应性变化的力量
senses.definition: the force that makes a population change its traits in order to cope with a new condition
senses.definitionCN: 使群体为应对新条件而改变性状的作用力
senses.example: The colder winters created adaptation pressure for thicker fur.
senses.exampleCN: 更冷的冬天形成了对更厚皮毛的适应压力。
senses.why: the phrase pictures a demand placed on a group: adjust or lose ground.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把一种要求压在群体上：要么调整，要么失利。

senses.title: An ecological mismatch that demands adjustment
senses.titleCN: 生态错配造成的调整需求
senses.definition: the strain produced when an organism's existing traits no longer fit its habitat
senses.definitionCN: 当生物原有性状不再适合其生境时产生的张力
senses.example: Earlier snowmelt put adaptation pressure on animals timed to the old season.
senses.exampleCN: 融雪提前对按旧季节计时的动物造成适应压力。
senses.why: the pressure is not a thing but a gap between what an organism has and what the place now asks for.
senses.whyCN: 这种压力不是实体，而是生物现有条件与地点新要求之间的落差。

senses.title: Evolutionary pressure toward a trait
senses.titleCN: 进化压力：促使性状形成
senses.definition: the evolutionary consequence of that demand, namely selection for a better-suited trait
senses.definitionCN: 这种需求在进化上的结果，即对更合适性状的选择
senses.example: Adaptation pressure over many generations produced the longer bill.
senses.exampleCN: 多代累积的适应压力造就了更长的喙。
senses.why: the demand becomes a genetic outcome only through selection, which is why the term sits close to selection pressure.
senses.whyCN: 需求只有通过选择才变成遗传结果，因此这个术语与选择压力靠得很近。

senses.title: An organisational adjustment demand
senses.titleCN: 组织层面的调整压力
senses.definition: pressure on an institution or company to change its structure or practice
senses.definitionCN: 迫使机构或公司改变结构或做法的压力
senses.example: New flood rules put adaptation pressure on the coastal towns.
senses.exampleCN: 新的防洪规定给沿海城镇带来适应压力。
senses.why: the ecological phrase is borrowed whenever an environment changes faster than the rules of the body inside it.
senses.whyCN: 只要外部环境变化快于内部规则，这个生态短语就会被借用。

senses.title: Climate-change pressure
senses.titleCN: 气候变化压力
senses.definition: the pressure exerted by shifting temperature, rainfall and sea level on species and settlements
senses.definitionCN: 温度、降水与海平面变化对物种和聚落施加的压力
senses.example: Rising seas are the sharpest adaptation pressure on the delta.
senses.exampleCN: 海平面上升是这片三角洲最尖锐的适应压力。
senses.why: climate change gives the term its most cited modern case: a moving baseline that no local adaptation can stop.
senses.whyCN: 气候变化提供了这个术语最常被引用的现代案例：一条本地适应无法阻止的移动基线。

senses.title: A demand for individual acclimatisation
senses.titleCN: 个体层面的适应需求
senses.definition: the strain on a single organism to adjust physiologically within its lifetime
senses.definitionCN: 单个生物在一生内进行生理调整所承受的张力
senses.example: Heat waves create adaptation pressure even in animals that can acclimatise.
senses.exampleCN: 热浪即使在能逐步适应的动物身上也造成适应压力。
senses.why: this sense marks the individual and short-term side, in contrast to the genetic and long-term side.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项标记个体与短期的一面，与遗传、长期的一面相对。

senses.title: Cultural or behavioural adjustment
senses.titleCN: 文化与行为层面的适应
senses.definition: pressure on people or communities to change practices, crops or routines
senses.definitionCN: 迫使人们或社区改变做法、作物或日常安排的压力
senses.example: The drying wells put adaptation pressure on farming practices.
senses.exampleCN: 水井干涸对耕作方式造成适应压力。
senses.why: human groups adapt by changing behaviour rather than genes, and the same phrase covers that route.
senses.whyCN: 人类群体靠改变行为而非基因来适应，同一个短语也覆盖这条路径。

senses.title: A term to be distinguished from selection pressure
senses.titleCN: 术语辨析：与选择压力不同
senses.definition: a cautionary sense in which the phrase stresses the need to adjust rather than the differential removal of variants
senses.definitionCN: 一个辨析义，强调「必须调整」而非「差别淘汰」
senses.example: Adaptation pressure describes a demand, while selection pressure describes its sorting effect.
senses.exampleCN: 适应压力描述的是一种需求，选择压力描述的是它的筛选效果。
senses.why: the two phrases overlap but are not synonyms, and writers who use them interchangeably blur demand with outcome.
senses.whyCN: 两个短语有重叠但并不等同，混用会把「需求」与「结果」搅在一起。

intro.en: The phrase joins adaptation, from Latin adaptare 'to fit to', to pressure, from Latin pressura 'a pressing'. Both parts are old words; the compound is modern, and dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把出自拉丁 adaptare「使适合」的 adaptation 与出自拉丁 pressura「压挤」的 pressure 组合起来。两部分都是旧词，复合词则是现代产物，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Aptus meant 'fitted, suited'; aptare meant 'to fit something to something else'.
items.cn: aptus 意为「合适的、契合的」；aptare 意为「把某物装到另一物上」。

items.en: Ad- 'to' plus aptare gave adaptare 'to fit to, adjust', the direct source of adapt and adaptation.
items.cn: ad-「向」加 aptare 得 adaptare「使适合、调整」，是 adapt 与 adaptation 的直接来源。

items.en: Adapt entered English in the seventeenth century; adaptation followed, at first meaning the act of fitting or the thing fitted.
items.cn: adapt 于 17 世纪进入英语，adaptation 随后出现，最初指「使适合」的行为或被改造成的东西。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology fixed adaptation as a trait that fits an organism to its conditions.
items.cn: 19 世纪生物学把 adaptation 固定为「使生物适合其条件的性状」。

items.en: The compound adaptation pressure is a twentieth-century formation, used chiefly in climate and conservation writing.
items.cn: 复合词 adaptation pressure 形成于 20 世纪，主要用于气候与保护类写作。

items.en: The exact first use of the compound is not recorded, and it remains less standard than selection pressure.
items.cn: 这一复合词的确切首用无记录，其标准化程度也不如 selection pressure。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same aptare family; group two holds near terms that describe demand, selection or the resulting trait.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 aptare 词族的形近词；第二组是近义术语，分别描述需求、选择或由此产生的性状。

entries.definition: Either the fitting process or the fitted trait. Adaptation pressure names only the demand that drives it.
entries.definitionCN: 既指适应过程，也指适应出来的性状；适应压力只指驱动它的那种需求。

entries.definition: To fit oneself or something else to conditions. It names the response, not the pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指使自己或他物适合条件；它命名的是回应，而非压力。

entries.definition: Describing a trait that improves survival. It says nothing about how hard the environment is pushing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容提高生存率的性状；不涉及环境推得有多狠。

entries.definition: Able to adjust to many conditions. It is a property of the organism, not a force acting on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指能适应多种条件；这是生物的属性，而非作用于它的力。

entries.definition: The force that removes some variants and keeps others. It describes the mechanism, while adaptation pressure describes the requirement.
entries.definitionCN: 指淘汰某些变异、保留另一些的作用力；它描述机制，而适应压力描述要求。

entries.definition: A condition that strains organisms, such as heat or salinity. It may generate adaptation pressure but is not identical with it.
entries.definitionCN: 指使生物受迫的条件，如高温或盐度；它可能产生适应压力，但不等同。

entries.definition: Adjustment within one lifetime, without genetic change. It is one response to adaptation pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指一生之内、无遗传改变的调整；它是对适应压力的一种回应。

entries.definition: The degree to which a system may be harmed. High vulnerability often means high adaptation pressure.
entries.definitionCN: 指系统可能受损的程度；高脆弱性往往意味着高适应压力。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: adapt 'fit to' + pressure 'pressing': the demand to fit.
normal.cn: adapt「使适合」+ pressure「压」：要求去适合。

normal.en: The family runs adapt, adaptation, adaptive, adaptable, pressure.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 adapt、adaptation、adaptive、adaptable、pressure。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: climate adaptation pressure, pressure on species, relieve pressure.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：气候适应压力、物种承受的压力、缓解压力。

normal.en: Pair it with selection pressure: one names the demand, the other the sorting.
normal.cn: 把它与 selection pressure 配对：一个命名需求，一个命名筛选。

normal.en: Pair it with vulnerability: exposure to harm is the practical face of the pressure.
normal.cn: 把它与 vulnerability 配对：易受损害是这种压力在实务上的面孔。

abstract.en: Picture two beak shapes on either side of a changing food supply.
abstract.cn: 想象食物改变后，两种喙形分列两侧。

abstract.en: Picture a town rebuilding its seawall higher each decade.
abstract.cn: 想象一座城镇每十年把海堤加高一次。

abstract.en: Picture a bird panting in shade while its body slowly adjusts.
abstract.cn: 想象一只鸟在阴影里喘息，身体慢慢调整。

examples.en: Rising temperatures place adaptation pressure on alpine plants.
examples.cn: 气温上升给高山植物带来适应压力。

examples.en: The pest's new host created adaptation pressure on the local beetles.
examples.cn: 这种害虫的新寄主对本地甲虫造成了适应压力。

examples.en: Planners treated migration as a response to adaptation pressure.
examples.cn: 规划者把迁徙视为对适应压力的一种回应。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「适应 + 压力」——环境变了，不换就得走 → 迫使调整的适应压力

root: 拉丁 ad-「向」+ aptare「使适合」（源自 aptus「合适的」）→ adaptare「使适合」；与拉丁 pressura「压挤」组合，20 世纪形成生态与气候术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one demand: conditions change, a gap appears, and the pressure is felt first as a force, then as a mismatch, a genetic outcome, an organisational demand, a climate signal, an individual strain, a cultural shift and finally a term to be kept distinct.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个需求展开：条件改变、落差出现，压力先表现为力，再表现为错配、遗传结果、组织要求、气候信号、个体紧张、文化转向，最后一个义项专门用于辨析。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a bird standing between a soft fruit and a hard-coated seed, its beak too shallow for one of them.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只鸟站在软果与硬壳种子之间，喙对其中一种来说太浅。

branches.en: THE GAP: changed conditions open a mismatch between what exists and what is asked.
branches.cn: 落差：条件改变在「现有」与「所需」之间打开一道错配。

branches.en: GENETIC OUTCOME: the demand is converted into selection for a better trait.
branches.cn: 遗传结果：需求被转换为对更佳性状的选择。

branches.en: HUMAN SCALES: organisations, coastlines and farming all feel the same demand.
branches.cn: 人的尺度：机构、海岸与农业都感到同一种需求。

branches.en: INDIVIDUAL: a single body adjusts within its lifetime.
branches.cn: 个体：单个身体在一生之内作出调整。

branches.en: DISTINCTION: the term names the requirement, not the sorting that follows.
branches.cn: 辨析：这个术语命名要求，而非随后的筛选。

intro.en: The compound joins a noun in -ation from adaptare to a noun in -ure from pressura; both halves remain free words.
intro.cn: 这个复合词把由 adaptare 派生、带 -ation 的名词与由 pressura 派生、带 -ure 的名词并置；两半仍是独立单词。

latinIntro.en: Latin aptare gives adapt, adaptation, adaptive, adaptable and aptitude; Latin premere gives press, pressure and compress.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aptare 衍生 adapt、adaptation、adaptive、adaptable 与 aptitude；拉丁 premere 衍生 press、pressure 与 compress。

items.example: Adaptation pressure rose as the river dried.
items.exampleCN: 随着河流干涸，适应压力上升。

items.example: The birds adapted to the harder seeds.
items.exampleCN: 这些鸟适应了更硬的种子。

items.meaning: the act of fitting; a fitted trait
items.example: The deeper bill is an adaptation to hard seeds.
items.exampleCN: 更深的喙是对硬种子的适应。

items.example: Adaptive radiation filled the empty niches.
items.exampleCN: 适应性辐射填满了空出的生态位。

items.example: The species is adaptable across latitudes.
items.exampleCN: 这个物种能跨纬度适应。

items.example: The finches show an aptitude for handling seeds.
items.exampleCN: 这些雀鸟在处理种子方面显出天赋。

items.example: The pressure came from the changed food supply.
items.exampleCN: 压力来自改变了的食物供给。

items.example: The layers compressed into limestone.
items.exampleCN: 这些层被压成石灰岩。

definition_en: the state of being physically healthy, the quality of being suitable, or in biology the relative reproductive success of a variant
core_image: 一只体态匀称的鹿站在坡上，旁边画着后代数量刻度与心率曲线，背景有哑铃剪影
scene: 同一片草场上有三只同种甲虫，各自留下的后代数量差了三倍。Reproductive fitness is measured not by how long an insect lives but by how many of its young survive.
sceneCN: 这里 fitness 指「（生殖）适应度」（第 3 个义项：个体在下一代基因库中所占的相对贡献）；句意：生殖适应度不看昆虫活多久，而看它有多少后代存活。图中可辨识物件：同种甲虫、后代数量刻度、存活率曲线、草场样方。

pos.zh: 健康；体能；适合；适应度（多为不可数）

derivatives.zh: 健康的；合适的 / 适合；安装

senses.title: Physical condition
senses.titleCN: 体能：身体状态良好
senses.definition: the condition of being physically healthy and strong
senses.definitionCN: 身体健康、有力的状态
senses.example: Regular hill walking improved his fitness within a season.
senses.exampleCN: 经常走山路使他的体能在一个季节内提高。
senses.why: fit first meant 'suited, well matched', and a body suited to its tasks came to be called fit.
senses.whyCN: fit 最初意为「合适的、匹配良好的」，适合其任务的身体便被称为 fit。

senses.title: Suitability or match
senses.titleCN: 适合：与用途相配
senses.definition: the quality of being suitable for a purpose or a position
senses.definitionCN: 适合某用途或某职位的性质
senses.example: The fitness of the site for a wetland was assessed first.
senses.exampleCN: 首先评估了该地块作为湿地的适合性。
senses.why: this is the oldest branch: a thing fits a slot, and its fittingness is its fitness.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一支：一物契合一个位置，其契合程度就是它的适合性。

senses.title: Evolutionary fitness
senses.titleCN: 进化适应度：后代的相对贡献
senses.definition: in biology, an individual's relative contribution of offspring to the next generation
senses.definitionCN: 生物学中个体对下一代基因库的相对后代贡献
senses.example: Fitness is measured relative to other individuals, not on an absolute scale.
senses.exampleCN: 适应度是相对于其他个体测量的，而非绝对尺度。
senses.why: biology took the 'goodness of fit' idea and made it about fit between organism and environment, expressed as offspring.
senses.whyCN: 生物学借用了「契合度」的概念，把它用于生物与环境之间的匹配，并以后代数量表达。

senses.title: Inclusive fitness
senses.titleCN: 广义适合度：含亲属的后代
senses.definition: the fitness gained through one's own offspring plus the offspring helped in relatives
senses.definitionCN: 由自身后代加上帮助亲属所增后代构成的适合度
senses.example: Helpers at the nest raise the inclusive fitness of their siblings.
senses.exampleCN: 巢边的帮手提高了其手足的广义适合度。
senses.why: once shared genes matter, helping a relative counts as part of one's own reproductive score.
senses.whyCN: 一旦共享基因被计入，帮助亲属也算进自身的繁殖得分。

senses.title: Fitness landscape
senses.titleCN: 适应度地形：把适合度画成山丘
senses.definition: a model that maps genotypes or traits onto reproductive success as a surface
senses.definitionCN: 把基因型或性状映射为繁殖成功的曲面模型
senses.example: The population climbed a local peak on the fitness landscape.
senses.exampleCN: 该群体在适应度地形上爬上一座局部山峰。
senses.why: the abstract score becomes a shape that can be walked, so peaks and valleys stand for good and poor combinations.
senses.whyCN: 抽象分数变成一个可行走的形状，峰与谷代表好与差的组合。

senses.title: Fitness testing and training
senses.titleCN: 体测与健身：日常健康语境
senses.definition: the everyday use for measured physical capacity and for gym training
senses.definitionCN: 日常语境中指可测量的身体能力与健身训练
senses.example: The team ran a fitness test before the season began.
senses.exampleCN: 赛季开始前球队做了体能测试。
senses.why: sport fixed the word to measurable capacity such as endurance and strength.
senses.whyCN: 体育把这个词固定到可测量的能力上，如耐力与力量。

senses.title: Statistical goodness of fit
senses.titleCN: 统计拟合优度：模型与数据的贴合
senses.definition: in statistics, how well a model or curve matches observed data
senses.definitionCN: 统计学中模型或曲线与观测数据的贴合程度
senses.example: The fitness of the model was poor at high temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型在高温下的拟合优度很差。
senses.why: the same 'fit' is used for a curve fitting points, with no biological content at all.
senses.whyCN: 同一个 fit 也用于曲线贴合数据点，完全不含生物学内容。

senses.title: Suitability for a post or role
senses.titleCN: 职位适合性：能否胜任
senses.definition: the quality of being qualified for a role or office
senses.definitionCN: 胜任某角色或职位的资格
senses.example: The committee questioned his fitness for the chair.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会质疑他是否适合担任主席。
senses.why: institutional life keeps the oldest sense alive: fitness is fitness for something named.
senses.whyCN: 制度生活保留了最古老的义项：适合性总是对某个被命名的东西而言。

intro.en: Fitness is fit plus -ness. The adjective fit has an uncertain origin, and the biological sense was fixed in the nineteenth century. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: fitness 由 fit 加 -ness 构成。形容词 fit 的来源不确定，生物学义在 19 世纪固定下来。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Fit appears in the thirteenth to fourteenth centuries meaning 'suitable, well matched'; its earlier origin is uncertain, and no source is agreed.
items.cn: fit 于 13 至 14 世纪出现，意为「合适的、匹配良好的」；其更早来源不确定，学界没有一致结论。

items.en: A separate noun fit meant a bout or a song, and some dictionaries suspect a link with the adjective; this remains a hypothesis, not a demonstrated source.
items.cn: 另有一个名词 fit 指一阵发作或一首歌，部分词典怀疑它与形容词有关；这仍属假说，而非已证实的来源。

items.en: Fitness is recorded in the sixteenth century as 'suitableness', before any health sense.
items.cn: fitness 于 16 世纪有记录，意为「合适」，早于任何健康义。

items.en: The 'physical condition' sense grows in the nineteenth century with organised sport and gymnasium culture.
items.cn: 「体能」义随 19 世纪有组织的体育与健身房文化而发展。

items.en: Darwin and Spencer made fitness a technical measure of reproductive success, later formalised as relative genetic contribution.
items.cn: 达尔文与斯宾塞把 fitness 变成繁殖成功的术语指标，后来形式化为相对基因贡献。

items.en: Source uncertain: the pre-English origin of fit is unknown, and any reconstructed form offered for it is speculative.
items.cn: 来源不确定：fit 在英语之前的来源不明，凡为它给出的重构形式均属推测。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the fit family and its homographs; group two holds measures and near terms from biology and sport.
note.cn: 第一组是 fit 词族及同形词的形近词；第二组是生物学与体育中的指标与近义词。

entries.definition: Healthy, suitable, or to make something match. Fitness is the noun of state built on it.
entries.definitionCN: 指健康的、合适的，或使某物相配；fitness 是由它构成的状态名词。

entries.definition: Either 'suitable' or the act of trying on clothes. It is not the biological measure.
entries.definitionCN: 或指「恰当的」，或指试衣；它不是生物学指标。

entries.definition: Not healthy or not suitable, the direct negation of fit.
entries.definitionCN: 指不健康或不合适，是 fit 的直接否定。

entries.definition: An old spelling of fitness found in sixteenth-century texts; it is the same word, not a variant sense.
entries.definitionCN: 16 世纪文本中的旧拼法；是同一个词，并非另一义项。

entries.definition: The same biological measure spelled out: relative contribution of offspring. It avoids confusion with gym fitness.
entries.definitionCN: 同一生物学指标的完整说法：后代的相对贡献；可避免与健身义混淆。

entries.definition: General physical and mental well-being. It is not a relative measure and carries no genetic meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 指总体的身心安好；不是相对指标，也不含遗传含义。

entries.definition: The state of a body or machine, often used in sport for endurance. It is broader than fitness and less measured.
entries.definitionCN: 指身体或机器的状态，体育中常指耐力；比 fitness 更宽泛、更少量化。

entries.definition: A fitted trait. Fitness is the reproductive score that such traits tend to raise.
entries.definitionCN: 指适应出来的性状；fitness 是这类性状往往会提高的繁殖得分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: fit 'suited' + -ness 'state': the state of being well matched.
normal.cn: fit「合适的」+ -ness「状态」：匹配良好的状态。

normal.en: The family runs fit, fitness, fitting, unfit, fitly.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 fit、fitness、fitting、unfit、fitly。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: physical fitness, fitness test, reproductive fitness, fitness landscape.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：体能、体能测试、生殖适应度、适应度地形。

normal.en: In biology, always ask what fitness is relative to; it has no absolute zero.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，总要问适应度是相对于谁；它没有绝对零点。

normal.en: Do not read reproductive fitness as physical health; the two senses are far apart.
normal.cn: 不要把生殖适应度读成身体健康；这两个义项相距很远。

abstract.en: Picture a key that turns smoothly in one lock and jams in another.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙在一把锁里顺滑转动，在另一把里卡住。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard that counts surviving young instead of years lived.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记分牌数的是存活后代而不是寿命。

abstract.en: Picture a hill map where each step uphill means more offspring.
abstract.cn: 想象一张山丘地图，每向上一步就意味着更多后代。

examples.en: Fitness in evolutionary biology is always relative to the rest of the population.
examples.cn: 进化生物学中的适应度总是相对于群体其余个体而言。

examples.en: Her fitness improved after three months of swimming.
examples.cn: 游了三个月后，她的体能提高了。

examples.en: The model's fitness to the data was tested at five sites.
examples.cn: 这个模型对数据的拟合优度在五个地点接受了检验。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「肥（fit）得合适」——身子合适叫健康，基因合适叫适应度 → 体能、适合、适应度

root: 英语 fit「合适的」+ -ness；fit 的英语之前来源不确定（相关假说均未证实）；生物学义由达尔文与斯宾塞在 19 世纪固定为繁殖成功的相对指标。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one idea: being well matched, whether a body to its tasks, a word to a post, an organism to its habitat, a relative's genes to yours, a model to data, or a curve to points.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个观念展开：匹配良好——身体与任务、人与职位、生物与生境、亲属基因与你、模型与数据、曲线与数据点。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a body that fits its work, with offspring counted beside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一副与工作相合的身体，旁边记着后代数量。

branches.en: BODY: health and measured capacity are the everyday face of being fit.
branches.cn: 身体：健康与可测能力是「合适」的日常面孔。

branches.en: SUITABILITY: the oldest sense, fitness for a purpose, a site or a post.
branches.cn: 适合性：最古老的义项，对用途、地块或职位的适合。

branches.en: REPRODUCTION: fitness becomes a relative count of descendants, own and shared.
branches.cn: 繁殖：适应度变成后代数量的相对计数，含自身与共享部分。

branches.en: MODEL: the score is drawn as a landscape of peaks and valleys.
branches.cn: 模型：得分被画成峰谷起伏的地形。

branches.en: STATISTICS: the same word measures how well a curve fits data.
branches.cn: 统计：同一个词衡量曲线与数据的贴合程度。

intro.en: Fitness is a short English adjective plus the native noun suffix -ness; it has no Latin affix structure of its own.
intro.cn: fitness 是简短英语形容词加本族名词后缀 -ness；它本身没有拉丁词缀结构。

latinIntro.en: The word has no Latin family; its relatives are English formations such as fitting, unfit and fitly.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词族；其同族词是 fitting、unfit、fitly 等英语构词。

items.example: Fitness varies with the environment.
items.exampleCN: 适应度随环境而变。

items.example: The seed is fit for dispersal by wind.
items.exampleCN: 这粒种子适合随风传播。

items.example: A fitting end to the dry season was a gentle rain.
items.exampleCN: 旱季的一个恰当收尾是一场细雨。

items.example: The wet field was unfit for grazing.
items.exampleCN: 湿透的田地不适合放牧。

items.example: The hut was fitly placed above the flood line.
items.exampleCN: 小屋恰当地建在洪水线之上。

items.example: The lighter seeds are fitter for wind travel.
items.exampleCN: 更轻的种子更适合随风传播。

items.example: The boat was refitted for the survey.
items.exampleCN: 这条船为调查重新装配。

items.example: The field outfit included nets and jars.
items.exampleCN: 野外装备包括网与罐。

definition_zh: 生殖适应度；个体把自身基因传给下一代的相对贡献
definition_en: the relative contribution an individual makes to the gene pool of the next generation through its offspring
core_image: 三只同种甲虫排成一排，头顶各标着不同数量的后代图标，最右边那只的后代图标排成一小串
scene: 实验箱里三只同种甲虫各留下不同数量的幼虫，最会产卵的那只后代最多。Reproductive fitness was scored as the number of larvae that survived to adulthood.
sceneCN: 这里 reproductive fitness 指「生殖适应度」（第 1 个义项：个体经后代对下一代基因库的相对贡献）；句意：生殖适应度以存活到成年的幼虫数量计分。图中可辨识物件：实验箱、甲虫、幼虫计数牌、存活率曲线。

pos.zh: 生殖适应度（不可数，作生物学术语）

senses.title: Relative genetic contribution
senses.titleCN: 相对基因贡献：在基因库中占多少
senses.definition: an individual's share of the next generation's gene pool compared with others
senses.definitionCN: 个体相对于他者，在下一代基因库中所占的份额
senses.example: Reproductive fitness is always a relative measure, not an absolute count.
senses.exampleCN: 生殖适应度始终是相对指标，而非绝对计数。
senses.why: the phrase joins the act of producing offspring to a score, so what is measured is a share rather than a quantity.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语把产生后代的行为与得分并置，因此测量的是份额而非数量。

senses.title: Lifetime number of offspring
senses.titleCN: 终生后代数：一辈子留下多少
senses.definition: the total number of offspring an individual produces over its whole life
senses.definitionCN: 个体一生所产生后代的总数
senses.example: Lifetime reproductive fitness differed sharply between the two morphs.
senses.exampleCN: 两种形态的终生生殖适应度差别很大。
senses.why: the score must be counted over a whole life, since early deaths and late broods both change the total.
senses.whyCN: 得分必须在整个生命期内计数，因为早亡与晚育都会改变总数。

senses.title: Survival to reproduction
senses.titleCN: 存活到繁殖：先活到能生育
senses.definition: the component of fitness that depends on reaching reproductive age
senses.definitionCN: 适应度中取决于能否活到繁殖年龄的那一部分
senses.example: A longer juvenile stage lowered reproductive fitness in the dry years.
senses.exampleCN: 幼期延长在干旱年份降低了生殖适应度。
senses.why: an organism that dies before breeding contributes nothing, so survival to maturity is a gate on the score.
senses.whyCN: 未繁殖即死亡的个体贡献为零，因此活到成熟是得分的一道门。

senses.title: Mating success as a component
senses.titleCN: 交配成功：找到配偶的组分
senses.definition: the part of fitness that comes from obtaining mates and fertilisation
senses.definitionCN: 适应度中来自获得配偶与成功受精的部分
senses.example: Display size raised mating success but not always reproductive fitness.
senses.exampleCN: 展示规模提高了交配成功率，但并不总能提高生殖适应度。
senses.why: mating is necessary but not sufficient: the score also depends on what happens after fertilisation.
senses.whyCN: 交配是必要而非充分条件：得分还取决于受精之后发生了什么。

senses.title: Inclusive fitness extension
senses.titleCN: 广义适合度：把亲属的后代计入
senses.definition: the extension of the score to include offspring of relatives that share the individual's genes
senses.definitionCN: 把共享其基因的亲属所育后代计入得分的扩展
senses.example: Inclusive fitness explains why some birds forgo their own nests.
senses.exampleCN: 广义适合度解释了为何有些鸟放弃自己筑巢。
senses.why: if genes are the currency, helping a sibling's young adds to the same account.
senses.whyCN: 若以基因为通货，帮助手足的幼鸟就等于往同一个账户里存钱。

senses.title: Measured proxies
senses.titleCN: 测量指标：窝仔数、存活率等
senses.definition: the practical quantities used to estimate fitness, such as clutch size or juvenile survival
senses.definitionCN: 用来估计适应度的实务数量，如窝卵数或幼体存活率
senses.example: Clutch size served as a proxy for reproductive fitness in the study.
senses.exampleCN: 在这项研究中，窝卵数被用作生殖适应度的替代指标。
senses.why: the full score is hard to count, so field studies measure parts of it and say so.
senses.whyCN: 完整得分难以计数，因此野外研究测量其部分，并如实说明。

senses.title: Trade-off with survival
senses.titleCN: 与生存的权衡
senses.definition: the tension between investing in current offspring and preserving the parent's future reproduction
senses.definitionCN: 投入当前后代与保全亲本未来繁殖之间的张力
senses.example: A heavy litter raised current output but lowered future reproductive fitness.
senses.exampleCN: 一窝过多的幼崽提高了当前产出，却降低了未来的生殖适应度。
senses.why: fitness is a lifetime total, so present success can be bought with future capacity.
senses.whyCN: 适应度是一生总数，因此当下的成功可能以未来的能力为代价。

senses.title: Misuse caution: not reproductive health
senses.titleCN: 误用警示：不等于生殖健康
senses.definition: a cautionary sense distinguishing the evolutionary score from medical fertility or well-being
senses.definitionCN: 一个辨析义，用于区分进化得分与医学上的生育力或健康
senses.example: A sterile worker can have high inclusive fitness despite zero personal fertility.
senses.exampleCN: 不育的工蜂个人生育力为零，却可以有很高的广义适合度。
senses.why: the term is about gene transmission, not about an individual's clinical condition.
senses.whyCN: 这个术语讲的是基因传递，而不是个体的临床状况。

intro.en: The phrase joins reproductive, from Latin reproducere 'to bring forth again', to fitness, an English noun of state. The biological phrase is a twentieth-century formation, and dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: 这个短语把出自拉丁 reproducere「再次产生」的 reproductive 与英语状态名词 fitness 组合起来；这一生物学短语形成于 20 世纪，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Ducere meant 'to lead'; producere 'to lead forward' is its compound with pro- 'forward'.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导」；producere「向前引出」是它与 pro-「向前」构成的复合词。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus producere gave reproducere 'to bring forth again', the source of reproduce and reproduction.
items.cn: re-「再一次」加 producere 得 reproducere「再次产生」，是 reproduce 与 reproduction 的来源。

items.en: Reproduce entered English in the seventeenth century for producing a copy; the biological sense is nineteenth-century.
items.cn: reproduce 于 17 世纪进入英语，指产生副本；生物学的繁殖义是 19 世纪的。

items.en: Fitness is a sixteenth-century English noun from fit plus -ness, first meaning 'suitableness'.
items.cn: fitness 是 16 世纪由 fit 加 -ness 构成的英语名词，最初意为「合适」。

items.en: Darwin and later population geneticists made reproductive fitness a relative count of descendants.
items.cn: 达尔文及后来的群体遗传学家把生殖适应度变成后代的相对计数。

items.en: The exact first use of the full phrase is not recorded, and its wording varies between reproductive fitness and relative fitness.
items.cn: 完整短语的确切首用无记录，其措辞也在生殖适应度与相对适应度之间变动。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes built from the same produce and fit words; group two holds related measures that answer a different question.
note.cn: 第一组是由 produce 与 fit 同一批词构成的形近词；第二组是回答不同问题的相关指标。

entries.definition: Can mean gym fitness or the biological score. Adding reproductive removes the ambiguity.
entries.definitionCN: 既可指健身体能，也可指生物学得分；加上 reproductive 便消除歧义。

entries.definition: Relating to reproduction, as in reproductive organs or reproductive success. It names no score by itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指与繁殖相关的，如生殖器官或繁殖成功；本身不指得分。

entries.definition: The act or process of producing offspring or copies. Fitness is the measure of its genetic result.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生后代或副本的行为与过程；fitness 衡量其遗传结果。

entries.definition: To produce offspring or a copy. It is the activity whose outcome the phrase scores.
entries.definitionCN: 指繁殖或复制；这个短语计分的是这一活动的结果。

entries.definition: Fitness compared with a reference genotype, often set to 1. It is the usual technical wording in population genetics.
entries.definitionCN: 指与参照基因型相比的适应度，常令参照值为 1；这是群体遗传学的常用术语。

entries.definition: The score extended to relatives' offspring. Reproductive fitness alone counts only one's own young.
entries.definitionCN: 把亲属后代计入的得分；仅说生殖适应度时只计自己的幼体。

entries.definition: The actual ability to produce young, used in medicine and demography. It is not a relative genetic measure.
entries.definitionCN: 指实际生育能力，用于医学与人口学；它不是相对的遗传指标。

entries.definition: The number of young raised. It is often used as a plain-language stand-in for fitness.
entries.definitionCN: 指育成的幼体数量；常用作适应度的通俗替代说法。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: reproduce 'bring forth again' + fitness 'score': the score earned by bringing forth young.
normal.cn: reproduce「再次产生」+ fitness「得分」：靠产生后代挣到的分。

normal.en: The family runs reproduce, reproduction, reproductive, fitness, fit.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reproduce、reproduction、reproductive、fitness、fit。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: lifetime fitness, relative fitness, inclusive fitness, fitness trade-off.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：终生适应度、相对适应度、广义适合度、适应度权衡。

normal.en: Always ask 'relative to whom' — the score has no absolute zero.
normal.cn: 总要问「相对于谁」——这个得分没有绝对零点。

normal.en: Distinguish it from fertility: a sterile worker ant can still score high through relatives.
normal.cn: 把它与生育力区分：不育的工蚁仍可通过亲属拿到高分。

abstract.en: Picture a scoreboard where each surviving chick adds a point.
abstract.cn: 想象一块记分牌，每只存活的雏鸟加一分。

abstract.en: Picture three beetles with ladders of offspring icons above them.
abstract.cn: 想象三只甲虫，头顶各有一列后代图标。

abstract.en: Picture an account where helping a sister's brood also pays in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个账户，帮姐妹育雏也能进账。

examples.en: Parasites often reduce the reproductive fitness of their hosts.
examples.cn: 寄生虫常降低宿主的生殖适应度。

examples.en: Inclusive fitness can be high even when personal offspring are few.
examples.cn: 即使亲生后代很少，广义适合度也可以很高。

examples.en: The team estimated lifetime reproductive fitness from banding records.
examples.cn: 团队依据环志记录估算终生生殖适应度。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「繁殖 + 得分」——把留下的后代当分数记在基因账本上 → 生殖适应度

root: 拉丁 re-「再一次」+ producere「向前引出」（pro- + ducere「引导」）→ reproducere「再次产生」；fitness 为英语 fit + -ness。二者组合为 20 世纪生物学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one ledger: a life produces young, the young are counted, survival and mating gate the total, relatives may add to it, proxies stand in, the future is traded against it, and the term is kept apart from clinical fertility.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一本账展开：一生育出后代，后代被计数，存活与交配把住总数，亲属可能加分，替代指标顶上，未来与当下相互交换，最后与临床生育力区分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of beetles above which offspring icons are tallied.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排甲虫上方，后代图标被逐一记账。

branches.en: THE SCORE: a relative share, counted over a whole life.
branches.cn: 得分：一份相对份额，在整整一生中计数。

branches.en: GATES: survival to breed and successful mating decide whether any points are earned.
branches.cn: 门槛：活到繁殖与成功交配决定是否挣到分。

branches.en: KIN: shared genes let relatives' young add to the same total.
branches.cn: 亲属：共享基因使亲属的幼体计入同一总数。

branches.en: PRACTICE: field proxies measure the score, and future reproduction is traded against present output.
branches.cn: 实务：野外指标测量得分，未来繁殖与当前产出相互交换。

branches.en: CAUTION: the evolutionary score is not a medical fertility diagnosis.
branches.cn: 警示：进化得分不是医学上的生育力诊断。

intro.en: The phrase joins a Latin-derived adjective in -ive to an English noun in -ness; the two halves come from different language layers.
intro.cn: 这个短语把带 -ive 的拉丁来源形容词与带 -ness 的英语名词并置；两半来自不同的语言层次。

latinIntro.en: Latin producere yields produce, product, production, reproduce and reproductive; fitness remains a native English formation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 producere 衍生 produce、product、production、reproduce 与 reproductive；fitness 仍是英语本族构词。

items.example: Reproductive fitness rose with larger clutches.
items.exampleCN: 生殖适应度随窝卵数增加而上升。

items.meaning: to produce offspring or a copy
items.example: The beetles reproduce once a year.
items.exampleCN: 这些甲虫一年繁殖一次。

items.example: Reproduction peaks in the wet season.
items.exampleCN: 繁殖在雨季达到高峰。

items.example: Reproductive organs were measured in the field.
items.exampleCN: 野外测量了生殖器官。

items.example: The meadow produces two hay crops.
items.exampleCN: 这片草甸一年产两茬干草。

items.example: Seed production depends on pollinators.
items.exampleCN: 种子生产依赖传粉者。

items.example: Fitness was scored relative to the reference line.
items.exampleCN: 适应度以参照系为基准计分。

items.example: The trait is fit for the new diet.
items.exampleCN: 这一性状适合新的食性。

definition_en: to produce offspring, to make a copy, or to present something again in another medium
core_image: 一台复印机吐出一叠一模一样的纸页，旁边另一条线索是一个细胞分裂成两个
scene: 复印室里机器一张接一张吐出与原件完全相同的纸页。The machine can reproduce the whole document in under a minute.
sceneCN: 这里 reproduce 指「复制」（第 2 个义项：把原件一模一样的副本造出来）；句意：这台机器能在一分钟内复制整份文件。图中可辨识物件：复印机、出纸口、相同的纸页、原件托盘。

pos.zh: 繁殖；复制；再现；重演（及物或不及物）

senses.title: Produce offspring
senses.titleCN: 繁殖：产生下一代
senses.definition: to produce young, seeds or new individuals
senses.definitionCN: 产生幼体、种子或新个体
senses.example: The plants reproduce by seed and by runners.
senses.exampleCN: 这些植物靠种子与匍匐枝繁殖。
senses.why: re- 'again' plus producere 'to bring forth' means one generation brings forth the next.
senses.whyCN: re-「再一次」加 producere「产生」，意思是一代产生下一代。

senses.title: Make an exact copy
senses.titleCN: 复制：造出一模一样的副本
senses.definition: to make a copy that matches an original
senses.definitionCN: 造出与原作一致的副本
senses.example: The archive reproduced the map at full size.
senses.exampleCN: 档案馆按原尺寸复制了那张地图。
senses.why: the same 'bring forth again' applies to an object: a second instance of the same thing.
senses.whyCN: 同一个「再次产生」也适用于物体：同一件东西的第二个实例。

senses.title: Repeat an experiment or result
senses.titleCN: 复现结果：让别人也能得到同样结果
senses.definition: to obtain the same result again, especially in a repeat of a study
senses.definitionCN: 再次得到相同结果，尤指重复一项研究
senses.example: Two labs failed to reproduce the original finding.
senses.exampleCN: 两个实验室未能复现最初的结果。
senses.why: science treats a result as real only if it can be brought forth again by others.
senses.whyCN: 科学只在他人能再次得到结果时才承认它成立。

senses.title: Play back sound or images
senses.titleCN: 播放：重现声音或影像
senses.definition: to render a recorded sound or image so that it can be heard or seen again
senses.definitionCN: 把录制的声音或影像再现出来，使人能重听或重看
senses.example: The speaker reproduced the call of the bird almost perfectly.
senses.exampleCN: 扬声器几乎完美地重现了鸟的鸣声。
senses.why: a recording is a second bringing-forth of an event that has already passed.
senses.whyCN: 录音是对已经过去的事件的一次「再次产生」。

senses.title: Represent in art
senses.titleCN: 再现：在艺术中表现对象
senses.definition: to depict or represent something in an artwork
senses.definitionCN: 在艺术作品中描绘或表现某物
senses.example: The mural reproduces the old market scene in detail.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅壁画细致地再现了旧日市集景象。
senses.why: art does not copy an object but brings its appearance forth again in another medium.
senses.whyCN: 艺术并非复制实物，而是在另一媒介中再次呈现它的外观。

senses.title: Recreate conditions
senses.titleCN: 重现条件：重建同一情境
senses.definition: to recreate the conditions under which something happened
senses.definitionCN: 重建某事发生时所处的条件
senses.example: The lab reproduced the drought in a controlled plot.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室在受控样地中重现了那次干旱。
senses.why: if conditions can be produced again, causes can be tested rather than merely observed.
senses.whyCN: 若条件能被再次造出，原因便可被检验，而不只是被观察。

senses.title: Self-replication of a system
senses.titleCN: 自我复制：系统复制自身
senses.definition: of a system, to make copies of itself, as in computer code or crystals
senses.definitionCN: 系统复制自身，如计算机代码或晶体
senses.example: The program reproduces itself in every new folder.
senses.exampleCN: 这个程序在每个新文件夹里自我复制。
senses.why: the biological image is borrowed for anything that leaves copies of its own pattern.
senses.whyCN: 生物意象被借用于任何留下自身模式副本的东西。

senses.title: Social reproduction of structures
senses.titleCN: 社会结构的再生产
senses.definition: in social theory, the process by which institutions and inequalities carry themselves forward
senses.definitionCN: 社会理论中制度与不平等把自己延续下去的过程
senses.example: Schooling can reproduce class differences across generations.
senses.exampleCN: 学校教育可能使阶级差异跨代延续。
senses.why: society is treated as a system that brings forth its own pattern again, often without anyone intending it.
senses.whyCN: 社会被当成一个系统，会再次产生自身的模式，且常无人有意为之。

intro.en: Reproduce comes from Latin reproducere 'to bring forth again', built on re- and producere 'to lead forward' from ducere 'to lead'. Dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: reproduce 出自拉丁 reproducere「再次产生」，由 re- 与 producere「向前引出」构成，后者源自 ducere「引导」。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Ducere 'to lead' is the stem behind produce, induce, reduce and conduct.
items.cn: ducere「引导」是 produce、induce、reduce 与 conduct 的共同词干。

items.en: Pro- 'forward' plus ducere gave producere 'to lead forth, bring out', the source of produce and product.
items.cn: pro-「向前」加 ducere 得 producere「引出、带出」，是 produce 与 product 的来源。

items.en: Re- 'again' plus producere produced reproducere 'to bring forth again'.
items.cn: re-「再一次」加 producere 构成 reproducere「再次产生」。

items.en: Reproduce entered English in the seventeenth century for making a copy; the biological sense is recorded in the nineteenth.
items.cn: reproduce 于 17 世纪进入英语，指制造副本；生物学义在 19 世纪有记录。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology fixed reproduce and reproduction as the terms for generating offspring.
items.cn: 19 世纪生物学把 reproduce 与 reproduction 固定为产生后代的术语。

items.en: The exact first citation and the timing of the shift from copying to breeding are uncertain.
items.cn: 确切的最早书证以及从「复制」转向「繁殖」的时间都不确定。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes from the same ducere family; group two holds near verbs that copy, repeat or breed.
note.cn: 第一组是同出 ducere 词族的形近词；第二组是近义动词，分别表示复制、重复或繁殖。

entries.definition: To make or yield something. Without re- there is no second instance.
entries.definitionCN: 指制造或产出某物；没有 re- 就不含第二个实例。

entries.definition: The act or result of reproducing. It names the process, while reproduce names the doing.
entries.definitionCN: 指繁殖或复制的行为与结果；它命名过程，reproduce 命名动作。

entries.definition: Relating to reproduction, as in reproductive system. It describes, it does not act.
entries.definitionCN: 指与繁殖相关的，如生殖系统；它描述而不施动。

entries.definition: From re- plus ducere 'to lead', but it means to lead back or down, not to bring forth.
entries.definitionCN: 同由 re- 加 ducere「引导」构成，但意为引回或降低，而非产生。

entries.definition: To make a duplicate of a document or object. It never means producing offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 指复制文件或物品；从不表示产生后代。

entries.definition: To produce young, especially under human management. It is narrower and often agricultural.
entries.definitionCN: 指产生幼体，尤指在人工管理下；范围更窄，常属农业语境。

entries.definition: To repeat an experiment or duplicate a molecule exactly. It stresses exactness more than reproduce does.
entries.definitionCN: 指重复实验或精确复制分子；比 reproduce 更强调精确。

entries.definition: To grow a lost part again. It is about repair of one body, not about producing a new one.
entries.definitionCN: 指重新长出失去的部分；讲的是一个身体的修复，而非造出新个体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- 'again' + producere 'bring forth': to bring forth another one.
normal.cn: re-「再一次」+ producere「产生」：再产生一个。

normal.en: The family runs produce, reproduce, reproduction, reproductive, reproducible.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 produce、reproduce、reproduction、reproductive、reproducible。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: reproduce successfully, reproduce the results, reproduce a sound.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：成功繁殖、复现结果、重现声音。

normal.en: In science, reproduce means another lab gets the same result.
normal.cn: 在科学中，reproduce 意味着另一个实验室得到同样的结果。

normal.en: In biology, reproduce means one generation makes the next.
normal.cn: 在生物学中，reproduce 意味着一代造出下一代。

abstract.en: Picture a photocopier stacking identical sheets.
abstract.cn: 想象复印机叠出一模一样的纸页。

abstract.en: Picture one cell pinching into two.
abstract.cn: 想象一个细胞收腰分成两个。

abstract.en: Picture a bird's song played back from a speaker.
abstract.cn: 想象鸟鸣从扬声器里被播放出来。

examples.en: These fish reproduce in the shallows every spring.
examples.cn: 这些鱼每年春天在浅水区繁殖。

examples.en: No other laboratory could reproduce the original measurement.
examples.cn: 没有其他实验室能复现最初的测量结果。

examples.en: The printer reproduces colour more accurately than the screen.
examples.cn: 这台打印机再现颜色比屏幕更准确。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「再（re）产（produce）」——再产一份：生后代，或印副本 → 繁殖、复制

root: 拉丁 re-「再一次」+ producere「向前引出」（pro- + ducere「引导」）→ reproducere「再次产生」；英语 17 世纪进入，生物学的繁殖义固定于 19 世纪。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one action: something is brought forth again, as young, as a copy, as a repeated result, as sound, as an image, as conditions, as a system's own pattern or as a social structure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：某物被再次产生——或是幼体，或是副本，或是重复的结果、声音、图像、条件、系统自身的模式或社会结构。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a copier and a dividing cell, both making a second instance.
core.cn: 核心意象：一台复印机与一个分裂的细胞，都在造出第二个实例。

branches.en: LIFE: one generation brings forth the next.
branches.cn: 生命：一代产生下一代。

branches.en: COPY AND IMAGE: an original is duplicated or depicted again.
branches.cn: 副本与图像：原件被复制，或被再次描绘。

branches.en: SCIENCE: a result or a condition is brought forth again so it can be tested.
branches.cn: 科学：结果或条件被再次造出，以便检验。

branches.en: PLAYBACK: recorded sound is heard again.
branches.cn: 播放：录下的声音被再次听到。

branches.en: SELF AND SOCIETY: systems leave copies of their own pattern, often unintended.
branches.cn: 自身与社会：系统留下自身模式的副本，往往并非有意。

intro.en: The verb is Latin re- plus producere, with the English verb ending -e; the noun shifts to -tion and the adjective to -ive.
intro.cn: 这个动词是拉丁 re- 加 producere，带英语动词词尾 -e；名词转为 -tion，形容词转为 -ive。

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere yields produce, reduce, induce, conduct and reproduce; producere adds product and production.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ducere 衍生 produce、reduce、induce、conduct 与 reproduce；producere 另加 product 与 production。

items.example: Ferns reproduce by spores.
items.exampleCN: 蕨类靠孢子繁殖。

items.example: Reproduction in the pond peaked in May.
items.exampleCN: 池塘里的繁殖在五月达到高峰。

items.example: The reproductive season is short.
items.exampleCN: 繁殖季很短。

items.example: The assay is reproducible across labs.
