definition_zh: 后代；子女；（动物的）幼崽；（植物的）子代
definition_en: the young produced by a parent, whether human, animal or plant
core_image: 一只母鸟站在巢边，三只张着嘴的雏鸟把头伸成一排，巢下散着碎蛋壳
scene: 巢边的母鸟把虫子塞进三张张开的嘴里，雏鸟的绒毛还没退。The offspring stayed in the nest for another three weeks before they could fly.
sceneCN: 这里 offspring 指「幼鸟；后代」（第 3 个义项：动物所产的幼体）；句意：这些幼鸟在巢里又待了三周才学会飞。图中可辨识物件：鸟巢、母鸟、三只雏鸟、碎蛋壳。

pos.zh: 后代；子女；幼崽（单复数同形）

senses.title: Biological descendants
senses.titleCN: 生物后代：延续下来的个体
senses.definition: the new individuals produced by a parent organism
senses.definitionCN: 亲本生物所产生的新的个体
senses.example: Each pair raised four offspring in the season.
senses.exampleCN: 每对鸟在这一季育出四只后代。
senses.why: off means 'away from' and spring means 'to arise', so the word pictures new life arising from a parent.
senses.whyCN: off 意为「离开」，spring 意为「涌出」，因此这个词描绘新生命从亲本涌出。

senses.title: A person's children
senses.titleCN: 子女：人的后代
senses.definition: the children of a person, used in formal or neutral writing
senses.definitionCN: 某人的子女，用于正式或中性写作
senses.example: The estate passed to his offspring.
senses.exampleCN: 这份产业传给了他的子女。
senses.why: the same word serves humans, which is why it appears in legal and formal prose where 'children' feels too warm.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也用于人，因此在法律与正式文本中取代了显得过于亲昵的「孩子」。

senses.title: The young of an animal
senses.titleCN: 动物幼崽：一窝里的幼体
senses.definition: the young of an animal, especially before independence
senses.definitionCN: 动物所产的幼体，尤指尚未独立时
senses.example: The fox moved her offspring to a new den at night.
senses.exampleCN: 母狐夜里把幼崽搬到新的洞穴。
senses.why: in zoology the word is neutral about number, so a whole brood can be called offspring.
senses.whyCN: 在动物学中这个词对数量中立，因此一整窝都可叫 offspring。

senses.title: A product or result, literary
senses.titleCN: 产物：文学化的「结果」
senses.definition: something that arises as a result of another thing, in elevated or literary use
senses.definitionCN: 由另一事物产生的结果，用于高雅或文学语境
senses.example: The theory was an offspring of wartime engineering.
senses.exampleCN: 这套理论是战时工程的产物。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps the parent-child shape and applies it to ideas and institutions.
senses.whyCN: 这个隐喻保留了亲子形状，并把它用到观念与制度上。

senses.title: Plant progeny
senses.titleCN: 植物子代：种子与幼苗
senses.definition: the seeds, seedlings or daughter plants produced by a parent plant
senses.definitionCN: 母株所产生的种子、幼苗或子株
senses.example: The orchard's offspring were planted in a new row.
senses.exampleCN: 果园的子代被栽到新的一行。
senses.why: botany extends the animal word to plants, where the 'young' may be a seed rather than a mobile creature.
senses.whyCN: 植物学把这个动物词扩展到植物，这里的「幼体」可以是一粒种子而非会动的生物。

senses.title: Hybrid progeny
senses.titleCN: 杂交后代：两个亲本的子代
senses.definition: the young produced by a cross between two varieties or species
senses.definitionCN: 两个品种或物种杂交所产生的子代
senses.example: The hybrid offspring were sterile in the first generation.
senses.exampleCN: 杂交后代在第一代是不育的。
senses.why: breeding needs a word that covers the result of a cross without naming the species.
senses.whyCN: 育种需要一个词来指杂交结果，而不点明物种。

senses.title: The filial generation in genetics
senses.titleCN: 遗传学中的子代：F1、F2
senses.definition: a generation in a breeding experiment, labelled F1, F2 and so on
senses.definitionCN: 育种实验中的一代，标记为 F1、F2 等
senses.example: The F1 offspring all showed the dominant trait.
senses.exampleCN: F1 子代全部表现出显性性状。
senses.why: experimental genetics counts generations, and offspring becomes a countable unit in a cross.
senses.whyCN: 实验遗传学按代计数，offspring 便成为杂交中的可数单位。

senses.title: A figurative successor
senses.titleCN: 比喻的继承者：事业的后来者
senses.definition: a person or group that continues an earlier person's work or tradition
senses.definitionCN: 延续前人或传统之工作的人或群体
senses.example: The new institute saw itself as the offspring of the old school.
senses.exampleCN: 新研究所把自己看作老学派的继承者。
senses.why: the last branch loosens biology entirely: what is inherited is a tradition rather than genes.
senses.whyCN: 最后一支完全松开生物学：被继承的是传统而非基因。

intro.en: Offspring is a native English compound of off 'away' and spring 'to arise, to leap up'. It has no Latin root, and dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: offspring 是英语本族复合词，由 off「离开」与 spring「涌出、跃起」构成。它没有拉丁词根，以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Old English ofspring meant 'children, descendants, fruit of the body', built from of 'from' and springan 'to spring, arise'.
items.cn: 古英语 ofspring 意为「子女、后代、身体的果实」，由 of「从」与 springan「涌出、产生」构成。

items.en: The verb springan meant 'to leap, burst forth, arise', and also gave the season name spring, when growth bursts out.
items.cn: 动词 springan 意为「跳跃、迸出、产生」，也给出季节名 spring，即万物迸发的时节。

items.en: The form settled as offspring, with the sense of a person's children or an animal's young.
items.cn: 形式固定为 offspring，指人的子女或动物的幼体。

items.en: Nineteenth-century biology made offspring a general term for the young of any organism, including plants.
items.cn: 19 世纪生物学使 offspring 成为任何生物（含植物）幼体的通称。

items.en: Breeding experiments gave the word a countable place in generation labels such as F1 offspring.
items.cn: 育种实验让这个词在 F1 子代等世代标记中获得可数位置。

items.en: First dates are approximate; the plural has been unchanged since Old English, and the form offsprings is rare and nonstandard.
items.cn: 首见年代为约数；复数自古英语起就不加 -s，offsprings 罕见且不合规范。

note.en: Group one holds look-alikes built from spring and off; group two holds near terms for the young of a parent.
note.cn: 第一组是由 spring 与 off 构成的形近词；第二组是近义术语，均指亲本所产的幼体。

entries.definition: A season, a coil, a water source or the act of leaping. Only in the compound does it mean descent.
entries.definitionCN: 指季节、弹簧、泉源或跳跃；只有在复合词中才表示血统。

entries.definition: A side branch of a plant or an organisation. It is derived from the same off-, but names a division rather than young.
entries.definitionCN: 指植物或组织的侧枝；同由 off- 构成，但指分支而非幼体。

entries.definition: A counterbalance, or a short shoot that roots beside the parent. It is not the general word for descendants.
entries.definitionCN: 指抵消，或母株旁生根的短枝；不是后代的通称。

entries.definition: The period when business or sport is quiet, built with off- meaning 'away from the main period'. It shares only the prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 指生意或赛事的淡季，off- 表「离开主要时段」；只共享前缀。

entries.definition: Away from the stage area, with off- meaning 'away'. The shared prefix is the only link.
entries.definitionCN: 指离开舞台区域，off- 表「离开」；只共享前缀而已。

entries.definition: Descendants treated as a group, from Latin progignere 'to bring forth'. It is more formal than offspring.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为群体的后代，出自拉丁 progignere「产生」；比 offspring 更正式。

entries.definition: The offspring of an animal while still young, or the state of being young. It is not used for human children in the same way.
entries.definitionCN: 指动物尚幼时的后代，或年轻的状态；不用于人的子女。

entries.definition: The plural of child, used for people and carrying an emotional tone that offspring lacks.
entries.definitionCN: child 的复数，用于人，带有 offspring 所缺的情感色彩。

entries.definition: A person or organism in a line of descent, possibly many generations later. Offspring usually means the immediate young.
entries.definitionCN: 指血统线上的一个人或生物，可能隔许多代；offspring 通常指直接的幼体。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: off 'from' + spring 'to arise': new life arising from a parent.
normal.cn: off「从」+ spring「涌出」：从亲本涌出的新生命。

normal.en: The family runs spring, offshoot, offset, offspring; progeny is a formal synonym.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 spring、offshoot、offset、offspring；progeny 是正式同义词。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the senses: produce offspring, viable offspring, number of offspring, offspring survival.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出义项：产生后代、可存活的后代、后代数量、后代存活。

normal.en: The plural never takes -s in standard use; offspring is already plural.
normal.cn: 标准用法中复数不加 -s；offspring 本身即复数。

normal.en: Genetics counts it by generation: F1 offspring, then F2.
normal.cn: 遗传学按代计数：先是 F1 子代，再是 F2。

abstract.en: Picture three open beaks in a nest, all pointed at one parent.
abstract.cn: 想象巢里三张张开的嘴，全都朝向同一只亲鸟。

abstract.en: Picture a seed dropping from a parent tree onto bare soil.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒种子从母树落到裸土上。

abstract.en: Picture a school of thought branching off an older one.
abstract.cn: 想象一个学派从更老的学派中分支出来。

examples.en: The pair produced six offspring over three breeding seasons.
examples.cn: 这对鸟在三个繁殖季里育出六只后代。

examples.en: Hybrid offspring often show traits intermediate between the parents.
examples.cn: 杂交后代常表现出介于两亲本之间的性状。

examples.en: The foundation regarded the new lab as its intellectual offspring.
examples.cn: 基金会把这个新实验室视为自己的学术后代。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「离开（off）母体、涌出（spring）的新生命」——从亲本身上冒出来的一代 → 后代

root: 古英语 of「从」+ springan「涌出、跃起」→ ofspring「子女、后代」；英语本族复合词，无拉丁词根；复数形式自古英语起不变。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one image: new life arises from a parent, as animals' young, people's children, plants' seed, hybrid crosses, experimental generations, or a tradition's successor.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个意象展开：新生命从亲本涌出——动物的幼体、人的子女、植物的种子、杂交子代、实验世代，或传统的继承者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: open beaks in a nest, all pointing at the parent bird.
core.cn: 核心意象：巢里张开的喙，全都朝向亲鸟。

branches.en: ANIMAL YOUNG: the literal descendants, counted as a brood.
branches.cn: 动物幼体：字面的后代，按窝计数。

branches.en: HUMAN CHILDREN: the same word in formal and legal prose.
branches.cn: 人的子女：同一个词用于正式与法律文本。

branches.en: METAPHOR: ideas, institutions and traditions arise from earlier ones.
branches.cn: 隐喻：观念、制度与传统由更早者产生。

branches.en: PLANTS: seed and seedling carry the line.
branches.cn: 植物：种子与幼苗延续血脉。

branches.en: BREEDING: crosses and labelled generations make the word countable.
branches.cn: 育种：杂交与世代标记使这个词可数。

intro.en: The word is a native English compound of a preposition and a verb stem; it takes no Latin prefix or suffix.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族复合词，由介词与动词词干构成；不含拉丁前缀或后缀。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin family. The nearest formal synonyms are borrowed: progeny from progignere and descendant from descendere.
latinIntro.cn: 它没有拉丁词族。最近的正式同义词是借来的：progeny 出自 progignere，descendant 出自 descendere。

items.example: The offspring dispersed along the river.
items.exampleCN: 后代沿河扩散。

items.meaning: to arise; the season of growth
items.example: New shoots spring from the burnt ground.
items.exampleCN: 新芽从烧过的地面涌出。

items.example: The club began as an offshoot of the society.
items.exampleCN: 这个俱乐部起初是该学会的分支。

items.example: The plant spreads by offsets.
items.exampleCN: 这种植物靠侧生短枝蔓延。

items.example: The progeny of one pair filled the pond.
items.exampleCN: 一对亲本的子代占满了池塘。

items.meaning: one in a line of descent
items.example: The villagers are descendants of the first settlers.
items.exampleCN: 村民是最早定居者的后裔。

items.meaning: a family of young hatched together
items.example: The brood left the nest in early June.
items.exampleCN: 这一窝幼鸟六月初离巢。

items.example: Each parent fed the chicks in turn.
items.exampleCN: 两只亲鸟轮流喂雏。
